sections.heading: Day 1: Saturday
sections.text: Our friendly staff welcomes you at the airport. Bus transfer from the airport to the marina. You will, then, be attributed to a cabin and discover the boat.

sections.heading: Day 2: Sunday
sections.text: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your program of the week, safety recommendations, and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook, and insurance will be checked for certified divers before leaving the marina. The captain will make his way to the first snorkeling site. It will also be possible to dive into this site for certified divers. The briefing of the so-called "check dive" will be presented to you by the guide. After lunch, you will sail south to the second snorkeling/diving site of the day. Before dinner, for those who wish, you can attend a presentation on the fauna and flora of the Red Sea. In the early evening, after dinner, the boat will continue south to reach the Sataya area overnight.

sections.heading: Day 3: Monday
sections.text: In the morning, the guide will tell you everything you need to know about “how to behave in the company of dolphins” for a respectful encounter with them. A first snorkeling trip with the dolphins will be organized. For certified divers who wish, a dive can be offered to you, outside the Sataya lagoon, where diving is prohibited. Not yet certified and want to discover the underwater world in scuba diving? Your guide can offer you an introduction to scuba diving. All you need to do is notify them early enough in the day so that they can adapt their program accordingly. Your guide will suggest several activities throughout the day. Diving, snorkeling along the reef, swimming, snorkeling with dolphins, the choice is yours. At night, a splendid starry landscape will occupy your evening after dinner.

sections.heading: Day 4: Tuesday
sections.text: After having enjoyed another moment of bliss with the dolphins in the morning, the captain and his crew will move the boat to one of the most beautiful sites of Fury Shoals. You will go on a snorkeling trip along the reef to observe the incredible biodiversity of the Red Sea. For certified divers, you will have the opportunity to immerse yourself in a magnificent coral garden. Depending on your wishes, a second dive can be organized in the afternoon on another Fury Shoals site, or a second excursion with the dolphins inside the lagoon of Sataya. Did you take photos during the day? A large screen awaits you in the lounge to present your photos to the whole group, your guide will be happy to comment on them after dinner.

sections.heading: Day 5: Wednesday
sections.text: Feel free to choose what you want to do: swim with dolphins, immerse yourself in one of the Fury Shoals sites, snorkel along a reef and observe the magnificent colors of the Red Sea, and make an intro dive. Your guide will adapt the program according to your wishes.

sections.heading: Day 6: Thursday
sections.text: After breakfast, a dolphin excursion and a dive for certified divers will be organized. You will then sail approximately 5 to 6 hours north to reach the site of Sheleneyat. You can snorkel along the reef. After dinner, time to party!

sections.heading: Day 7: Friday
sections.text: At the break of dawn, the boat will sail to the Ras Galep area where you will go diving or snorkeling on the two sites selected by your guide. You will arrive at the marina early in the afternoon. Your guide will tell you all about the leisure activities you can book in the Marsa Alam area to spend an entertaining Friday afternoon.

sections.heading: Day 8: Saturday
sections.text: Departure from the boat will be, after breakfast or according to your flight and transfer schedules to the airport or hotel. Note: This program may be subject to changes according to the conditions. Supervised snorkeling by a certified instructor. 1 intro dive per person (DSD). For certified divers, 1 dive per day from Sunday to Friday. Come and discover the sumptuous seabed of the Red Sea through the Fury Shoals sites. Sataya is a crescent-shaped reef that stretches 2 kilometers long and is home to hundreds of spinner dolphins. You will stay there for at least 3 days and you will be able to fulfill an old childhood dream: swimming with the dolphins! You will be accompanied by our experienced guides who will share with you the awareness of fauna and flora, and the respect for the marine environment. Children will be supervised by one of our monitors and several activities will be offered to them throughout the week : Trips with dolphins, fins-mask-snorkel Discovery of diving from 8 years old Games and swimming times Activities on the boat Slideshow on flora and fauna commented on by our guide You can evolve into snorkeling on the diving sites. You will also have the possibility of doing one or more Scuba Diving discoveries. Certified divers are also welcome! Contact us for children under 14, a reduction is applicable.

sections.heading: This diving safari takes you to discover the most famous Egyptian dive sites.
sections.text: You will make fabulous dives on the most legendary sites of Egypt. The name Golden Triangle refers to the geographical position of the dive sites that will be visited during the cruise, placed in the shape of a triangle.

sections.heading: These three dive sites are :
sections.text: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef, ...hence the acronym BDE.

sections.heading: The Brothers Islands
sections.text: are two islands located 60 km off the coast of Al Qseir in Egyptian territorial waters. These islands are made of volcanic rocks. Big Brother is approximately 600m long and topped by a lighthouse built by the British in the 19th century. 4 keepers ensure the lighthouse operates properly and will be happy to welcome you for a visit. In the north of the island are 2 beautiful wrecks that you can discover during your dives: the Numidia (1901) is lying almost vertically against the reef between 10m and 83m and is covered with colorful corals. The Aida II (1958), a military ship supplying the Brothers Islands and bringing the new lighthouse keepers, sank 100m away from the Numidia and lay between 10m and 63m. In this area, you can have the opportunity to encounter a thresher shark... Small Brother is about 200m long. You will see, among other things, a beautiful garden of gorgonian sea fans, black corals, and many pelagic fishes.

sections.heading: Daedalus Reef
sections.text: is 600m long and 300m wide. It lies about 90km off the coast, south of Marsa Alam. It is topped by a lighthouse built by the French in 1863 and modified by the British in 1931. It is also possible to visit the lighthouse and enjoy its breathtaking view of the magnificent reef of Daedalus. At least ten different dives can be organized on this reef that has the greatest coral diversity in the Egyptian Red Sea. North of the reef, a school of hammerhead sharks is very often seen. A large number of pelagic fishes and varied fauna will enhance your dives.

sections.heading: Elphinstone
sections.text: is 400m long and 30m wide. Strong currents hit the northern and southern plateau bringing nutrients to a vast colony of soft corals. Many shark species, among which the oceanic white tip shark (Carcharhinus longimanus) are seen in the area. Let yourself be carried away by the currents and enjoy the abundant pelagic fauna. sections.heading: St John's Reef
sections.text: offers a large number of dive sites that look like submarine islands. This set of reefs lies

sections.heading: 200 km South of Marsa Alam
sections.text: , on the tropic of Cancer in the southern part of the Egyptian Red Sea. Pristine drop-offs covered with hard and soft corals, gardens of gorgonian sea fans, a huge variety of pelagic fishes, and a visibility of 50+ meters is what you will be thrilled to find there. The colorful coral gardens and their pinnacles resting on a sea bed made of white sand, the anemones, and their clown fish, the pelagic fishes slowly cruising the blue: your breath will surely be taken away! Whether you are an amateur or truly fond of marine biology, a photographer or video maker, do not search any longer. This itinerary is what you are looking for!

sections.heading: THE IDEAL ITINERARY FOR LOVERS OF WRECKS AND BREATHTAKING DROP-OFFS!
sections.text: Embark on an adventure with our new itinerary, still largely unexplored, offering an incredible diversity of dive sites. This is a route where you'll feel like an explorer. A 7-night itinerary focused on the area around Dahab and the islands of Tiran. These are renowned dive sites yet still untouched by cruise boats. Spend a week in total immersion, discovering the gems of the northern Red Sea in Egypt.

sections.heading: Day 1: Arrival
sections.text: Our team will welcome you at the airport. You will be transferred by bus to the marina. Your cabin will then be assigned, and you can begin to explore the boat.

sections.heading: Day 2: Departure from Safaga
sections.text: After breakfast, a welcome briefing will be presented by the guide, covering the week's organization, onboard safety instructions, etc. Your diving documents and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The captain will set course to the first diving site, which is 30 minutes from departure, where the briefing for the "refresher" dive will be conducted. After lunch, you will perform the second dive of the day in the Hurghada area before continuing your journey north to reach the area of El Gouna, where you will spend the night at a site sheltered from the waves.

sections.heading: Day 3: Tiran
sections.text: On this third day of the cruise, you will have the opportunity to explore the island of Tiran. Located near the tip of Sinai, this island offers three unique dives at three different sites. The first diving site, Thomas Reef, features a rich drop-off and a plateau to the west, where you may be lucky enough to spot sharks. You will then dive at Jackson Reef, followed by a dive at Gordon Reef. Afterward, you will head towards Ras Abou Gallum.

sections.heading: Day 4: Ras Abou Gallum
sections.text: Early in the morning, you will perform your first dive at Ras Abou Gallum. Three dives are offered in this protected area, teeming with life. The first dive will explore a drop-off, while the next two dives will take you through magnificent coral gardens.

sections.heading: Day 5: Dahab
sections.text: On this fifth day of the cruise, you will have the opportunity to explore the internationally renowned Blue Hole of Dahab, a premier diving and snorkeling site. Next, you will dive at a site known as the Canyon, followed by a third dive at the Island, a stunning coral garden that is sure to impress.

sections.heading: Day 6: Nabq
sections.text: Today, you will spend time in the Nabq area. Your first dive will be at the beautiful Gabr El Bent site, featuring a breathtaking drop-off and lagoon. A second dive will take place at the Abu Syela site, a magnificent coral garden. Finally, you will end your day with a drift dive at Gabr El Bent Alshogayrat.

sections.heading: Day 7: Safaga
sections.text: The last two dives of the week will be conducted in Safaga, depending on the return marina. Stunning drop-offs await to make a grand finale of your week. The boat is scheduled to return in the afternoon. You will have the opportunity to rinse your equipment on the rear platform of the boat or take a stroll in Safaga. Depending on your flight schedule, other activities may be offered to fully enjoy your Friday afternoon.

sections.heading: Day 8: Departure
sections.text: Depart from the boat after breakfast, or earlier, depending on your transfer time to the airport or hotel. (*) itinerary description provided by the boat operator. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

dune-silky::North Ras Mohammed (Safaga -.intro: For history and wreck lovers, this cruise in Egypt is made for you! Accessible from level 1, you will discover ships dating back more than a century, warships, including the mythical wreck of the Thistlegorm, and all this in the 10 meters to 30 meters depth zone. You will evolve in the magnificent National Park of Ras Mohamed 480 sq km between land and sea. This reserve offers us extraordinary fauna and contains one of the most beautiful coral ecosystems in the world. There are more than 150 species of corals, as well as remarkable marine fauna.

dune-silky::St John's Reef (Marsa Ghalib.intro: Discover the most beautiful sites of the southern Egyptian Red Sea. If you are a thrill seeker, come aboard one of our boats for an exceptional itinerary. From Port Ghalib, you will sail to the famous Daedalus reef where you will start your stay to meet the pelagics. You will continue your adventure towards the Rocky and Zabargad islands, where a feeling of the end of the world awaits you. Moreover, Zabargad is known to shelter an important population of turtles which come to lay their eggs there! Then you will head towards the St John's area, with its multicolored reefs and its surprising coral structures. On the way up, you will pass by Sataya, the largest reef in Egypt, with a lagoon where many dolphins come to rest during the day. Finally, you will end your stay on the exceptional site of Elphinstone, teeming with life and swept by the currents... You will have understood, that this itinerary gathers all that you can dream of in the Red Sea.

After lunch, you will sail for about two hours heading south to reach the dive site called “Gota Sharm” where you will do your second dive. After dinner, the boat will sail all night long, crossing the Tropic of Cancer on its way, to reach the Saint John's reef area at the break of dawn.

sections.text: Saint John's Reef : 3 dives will be organized and, upon request, a night dive may be added. The sailing time between the dive sites varies from 30 min to 1h30. For a quiet and peaceful night, you will spend the night moored behind a big reef.

sections.heading: Day 4: Saint John's
sections.text: At sunrise, the captain and his crew will take you to another fantastic dive site of Saint John's Reef for another great day of diving. Upon request, a night dive may be added.

sections.heading: Day 5: Saint John's & Fury Shoals
sections.text: You will do two-morning dives before sailing up north. 4 hours later you will reach “Sataya” (Dolphin House) in the Fury Shoals area. According to your time of arrival and the light, you will have the opportunity to go snorkeling with dolphins. The third dive of the day will take place in daylight, at dusk, or at night. The boat will be moored on Sataya Reef for the night.

sections.heading: Day 6: Fury Shoals & Sheleneyat
sections.text: You will do two dives on two beautiful reefs of the Fury Shoals area. After lunch, the boat will head north for a 6-hour sail to reach the site called “Shelinyiat”. The third dive of the day will either take place in daylight, at dusk, or at night according to your time of arrival. After dinner, the captain and his crew will organize a surprise Egyptian event.

sections.text: The boat will sail for 45 min before you reach your first dive site of the day. sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: The Brothers are 2 islands located 60 km off the village of Quseir, in Egyptian territorial waters. These islands are made up of volcanic rocks. On the approximately 600 m long large island is a lighthouse built in the 19th century by the English. 4 guards on-site ensure its proper functioning and are delighted to welcome you for the visit to the lighthouse. To the north of the island are 2 beautiful wrecks that you can discover during your dives. Numidia (1901) very concretion, is between 12 and 83 meters deep. The wreckage is almost vertical. A vertiginous dive on a very colorful drop-off. The Aïda 2 (1958), an Egyptian army boat supplying the islands and carrying the relief of the guards, is barely 100 meters from the Numidia at a depth of 30 to 63 m. It is not uncommon to come across a thresher shark in this area. The small island, made of the same rock as the big one, is about 200 m long. It's a real nugget. Between the Gorgonian garden, black coral, and passage of pelagics, you will be enchanted by the richness of this reef.

This reserve offers us extraordinary fauna and contains one of the most beautiful coral ecosystems in the world. There are more than 150 species of corals, as well as remarkable marine fauna.

dune-titan::Safaga Routes (Safaga - Safa.intro: How great it is to be on the boat every night to watch the stars... This liveaboard safari is for you! On your own to blow your first bubbles, with your family or a group of friends, you will be delighted by the splendid coral gardens, the pristine drop-offs covered in soft corals, or the world-renowned shipwreck of the

sections.heading: Salem Express
sections.text: . Your guide will give you a presentation on the flora and fauna of the Red Sea, an Egyptian party will be thrown during the week, as well as extra-diving activities. Do you wish to organize a trip with your dive club, to complete your diving courses in a perfect environment with your own instructors? It is now possible in

sections.heading: Safaga
sections.text: . We can provide you with a liveaboard safari boat and a guide to simplify communication with the crew. You will then be able to choose the sites you wish to dive for your training courses: shallow waters or drop-offs, the site is distant with about one hour of navigation. Our guide will be there to organize whatever you may wish in terms of diving. For example, you can organize two technical dives in the morning and an exploration in the afternoon plus one or two night dives during the week. This liveaboard is also open to snorkelers, free divers, and to beginners who wish to train. Navigations between the dive sites are very short and the bay of

dune-titan::St John's Reef (Marsa Ghalib.intro: Discover the most beautiful sites of the southern Egyptian Red Sea. If you are a thrill seeker, come aboard one of our boats for an exceptional itinerary. From Port Ghalib, you will sail to the famous Daedalus reef where you will start your stay to meet the pelagics. You will continue your adventure towards the Rocky and Zabargad islands, where a feeling of the end of the world awaits you. Moreover, Zabargad is known to shelter an important population of turtles which come to lay their eggs there! Then you will head towards the St John's area, with its multicolored reefs and its surprising coral structures. On the way up, you will pass by Sataya, the largest reef in Egypt, with a lagoon where many dolphins come to rest during the day. Finally, you will end your stay on the exceptional site of Elphinstone, teeming with life and swept by the currents... You will have understood, that this itinerary gathers all that you can dream of in the Red Sea.

Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. After lunch, you will sail for about two hours heading south to reach the dive site called “Gota Sharm” where you will do your second dive. After dinner, the boat will sail all night long, crossing the Tropic of Cancer on its way, to reach the Saint John's reef area at the break of dawn.

sections.heading: Day 3: Saint John's Reef
sections.text: Saint John's Reef : 3 dives will be organized and, upon request, a night dive may be added. The sailing time between the dive sites varies from 30 min to 1h30. The dive sites are carefully selected by your guide according to the weather forecast and the number of boats already moored on the site. For a quiet and peaceful night, you will spend the night moored behind a big reef.

sections.heading: Day 4: Saint John's
sections.text: At sunrise, the captain and his crew will take you to another fantastic dive site of Saint John's Reef for another great day of diving. Upon request, a night dive may be added.

sections.text: You will do two-morning dives before sailing up north. 4 hours later you will reach “Sataya” (Dolphin House) in the Fury Shoals area. According to your time of arrival and the light, you will have the opportunity to go snorkeling with dolphins. The third dive of the day will take place in daylight, at dusk, or at night. The boat will be moored on Sataya Reef for the night.

sections.text: You will do two dives on two beautiful reefs of the Fury Shoals area. After lunch, the boat will head north for a 6-hour sail to reach the site called “Shelinyiat”. The third dive of the day will either take place in daylight, at dusk, or at night according to your time of arrival. After dinner, the captain and his crew will organize a surprise Egyptian event.

sections.heading: Daedalus, Fury & Elphinstone:
sections.text: Elphinstone, Daedalus, Fury Shoals Sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals, elegant red gorgonians, vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves, and drop-offs at Elphinstone. Likely oceanic white tip encounters. Mountainous Daedalus with pristine, hard coral formations and a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks. Fury Shoals, a vast reef system to explore, such as Sataya’s resident spinner dolphins, famous swim-throughs and huge porites corals at Sha’ab Claude, mazes and friendly turtles, fantastic coral gardens, and much more that will simply blow you away!

sections.heading: Day 1: Check Dive & Depart
sections.text: Guests arriving at the required airport on the check-in day will be met by a representative, wearing a uniform and holding a sign representing the boat for your trip. Check-in: We leave the port as soon as all the clients are on board.

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: This trip offers you some of the best diving in the Red Sea and includes Daedalus, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone. With less distance to travel than some routes, you have more time to dive these iconic sites, and there is less chance of seasickness with shorter sailings and secure moorings. Depending on prevailing weather conditions, your guides will pick sites suitable for night dives outside the Marine Park. Heading first to Fury Shoals, we may dive around the Marsa Alam area or perhaps dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. Oceanic white tips and silky sharks can sometimes be found in the blue, and turtles often visit the south side before heading further south. At Fury Shoals, we have more time to explore the vast reef system than other itineraries afford. Of course, we will dive the classics such as Sha’ab Claude (a.k.a. Claudio) with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals, Malahi with its mazes and friendly turtles, and Abu Galawa Soraya with its fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat smothered with glass fish. Sataya with its resident spinner dolphin population is a must for snorkelling between dives, as well as having some good underwater offerings, and on top of that we can spend time exploring less dived sites such as Sha’ab Hamam (Stairway to Heaven), Abu Galawa Kebir with the Tien Hsing wreck, Gota Sataya and if the weather is kind there are some submerged reefs that can be moored on such as Habili Sameh that will blow you away! Daedalus Reef, part of the Red Sea offshore Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads, especially from May to November, and grey reef sharks. Of course, no trip to the South would be complete without stopping at world-famous Elphinstone, with its sheer walls covered in soft corals, and likely encounters with oceanic white tip sharks. Depending on the experience of the group and the weather, you may even get the chance to dive it at the beginning and end of your amazing trip!

We return to port at approximately 1 pm and moor here overnight. Evening-time pack up diving equipment, visit the marina, and settle any outstanding bills, ready to depart for the airport or hotel the following morning.

sections.text: Check-out begins early morning on the day of disembarkation, with all guests departing by midday.

Divers can explore colorful coral gardens, towering walls, and intricate reef mazes bursting with life. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. sections.heading: Simply the Best:
sections.text: Elphinstone, Brothers, Daedalus Reef Explore the wreck graveyard at Abu Nuhas, visit the infamous SS Thistlegorm and sister Rosalie Moller, Salem Express, and more. Breath-taking reefs and fishes at Shark & Yolanda at Ras Mohamed National Park, magnificent anemones and huge coral formations at Panorama Reef, Safaga Deep walls draped in soft corals and gorgonian forests take centre stage to diverse marine life and large pelagics at the Brothers. Look out for big tuna, barracudas, jacks, and snappers. Occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tips, mantas, and the rare chance to spot the thresher shark.

sections.heading: Day 1: Check Dive & Depart

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: Starting from Hurghada, we sail north towards Gubal Island and on to Abu Nuhas and its four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the ‘Lentil Wreck’ and the ‘Tile Wreck’, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life. Explore the Rosalie Moller (the sister ship of the slightly more famous Thistlegorm), which lies from 30 to 50 metres deep and is in excellent condition. Although the visibility is not always good, the wreck is covered in glassfish from bow to stern, and hunting them are masses of lionfish. Around the wreck are the usual pelagics such as tuna, trevallies, Emperor fis,h and many more. A short ride across the Straits of Gubal and you visit the most famous wreck of the Red Sea, the SS Thistlegorm! An awe-inspiring World War II British vessel with a cargo full of armaments, Bedford trucks, and BSA motorbikes, which were all destined for the British troops in North Africa. She was sunk by the German Luftwaffe and now lies in 30 metres of water. Depending on divers’ experience, along with weather and current conditions, we try to offer a night dive here. Nearby is the Ras Mohamed National Park, offering a morning dive at the renowned ‘Shark and Yolanda’ reefs. Ras Mohamed National Park is the furthest Sinai destination before heading south towards the Brothers. The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore from El Quseir. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Big tuna, barracudas, jack,s and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can sometimes be found there. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother. For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks. The boat will then sail back to Hurghada via Safaga, where you can dive at Panorama Reef or the famous wreck of Salem Express for a memorable finale!

sections.heading: Brother Islands
sections.text: are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Large tuna, jacks, and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silvertips, silky and oceanic white tip sharks, and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can be found here. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother. For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks.

sections.heading: Daedalus Reef
sections.text: , also part of the Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks.

sections.heading: Elphinstone
sections.text: is approximately 30km from Port Ghalib; Elphinstone reef is 300 metres long with sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals and elegant red gorgonians descending to around 40 metres. Other areas of the reef have near-vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves, and drop-offs of up to 100 metres. Elphinstone is known to experience some strong currents attracting many diverse species such as barracuda, angel fish, groupers, Napoleons, morays, reef sharks, and great shoals of dogtooth tuna and jacks. Occasional sightings include dolphins, turtles, oceanic white tip, and hammerhead sharks.

sections.heading: Itinerary Highlights
sections.text: Spoilt for choice with 21+ DIVES at the most remote and rewarding reef systems of the south A less arduous itinerary for a more relaxed diving pace Stunning typography with coral gardens, walls, overhangs, and swim-throughs Expect to see turtles, sharks, grey reef sharks, reef fishes, macro, shoals of glass fish, snappers, butterfly fish, and barracuda This trip takes you to some of the best diving the Red Sea has to offer. Here, diving is less arduous, so it’s a trip for those who want to see the best but have a more relaxed time while doing so. As a 21+ DIVES cruise, there’s a good chance to enjoy 21 or more dives on a 7-day safari if you choose to. Sailing to the southernmost reefs, you’ll depart from Port Ghalib and dive some sites to the South before sailing overnight to your southernmost point in the St. John’s area. Depending on weather, government approval, and marine life sightings in recent weeks, we may sail to the southernmost islands of Rocky and Zabargad, or we’ll moor instead in the vast reef system of St John’s to begin the adventure in the South. When leaving Port Ghalib, the route can sometimes dive Abu Dabab on the first or last day. Often spoilt for choice, your guides will pick sites that they know to be the best for the time of year and can find excellent alternatives should the weather affect the normal route. Although the distances are long, where possible, we travel overnight, so, as a 21-plus route, we aim to get as many dives in as possible at some of the most impressive reefs. Below are some of the highlights. On the way to Fury Shoals, we’ll dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. At Fury Shoals, dive Sha’ab Claude with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals. White tip reef sharks and an anemone, and a clownfish settlement can be seen a little off the reef to the South. Abu Galawa Soraya has a fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat populated with glass fish. St John's is a vast collection of small reefs offering some of the most remote and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. This incredibly beautiful reef lies a short distance north of the Sudanese border. The reef covers a huge area, and many dives would be needed to explore the numerous coral heads and islands. Habili Ali offers giant gorgonians and black corals, whilst grey reef, silvertip, and schools of hammerhead sharks might be found on the west side. Habili Gafaar is a mass of soft corals teaming with shoals of snappers, butterfly fish, and barracudas. Mantas, grey ree, and silvertip sharks can often be seen in the blue. Gota Kebir is a massive reef, famous for its tunnels and south plateau, where jacks and barracudas can be seen, and the occasional manta. The tunnels are ideal for novice cave divers. Gota Soraya is rated as possibly one of the best wall dives in the Red Sea, with overhangs and cracks in the reef wall full of glass fish and sweepers and an abundance of corals, Grey Reef, Silvertips, and Hammerhead sharks. On the last day as we head back to port, we will try to take in a dive or two on the world famous Elphinstone Reef if weather and diver experience permits us, or we will finish in the Abu Dabab area perhaps with another dive or two closer to Port Ghalib to relax and unwind before your final night in port. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator.

sections.heading: Southern Solitude:
sections.text: Elphinstone, Daedalus, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, Abu Dabab Going ‘against the flow’ to see the best sites in the southern Red Sea at their quietest times. Elphinstone, Daedalus, and St John’s at their quietest, with the rarely-dived sites of Rocky and Zabargad also included. This is a 21+ itinerary with all dives made offshore. By staying out of port on the last night, there’s potential for up to 22 dives on the trip – the most any of our itineraries offer. A diverse range of marine life, such as tuna, barracudas, jacks, groupers, Napoleon, bumphead parrotfish, and sharks, including hammerheads and occasionally silky and oceanic white tips. Dolphins and turtles in the Fury Shoals, while manta, thresher sharks, and whalesharks can always surprise. This fantastic itinerary gives divers the wonderful opportunity to ‘go against the flow’ and dive the best sites of the Red Sea on what should be their quietest days. By approaching these iconic sites in the opposite direction to most standard itineraries, we hope to offer you the best chance to dive with the fewest number of people around you.

sections.heading: Day 1: Check Dive & Depart

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: Southern Solitude is a dive-focused trip, heading out of Port Ghalib and immediately arriving in the Elphinstone area. This enables us to make a check dive nearby and then get straight to a site which is normally frequented on the final days of trips. With fewer boats around, it should give the chance to enjoy the 300-metre-long reef’s colourful pink and red soft coral sheer walls in relative peace and quiet. We’ll then go to Daedalus, arriving before most others, to take in its deep walls and drop-offs, which offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found, before heading down to the exceptionally remote, and usually quiet, Rocky and Zabargad Islands, where even many Red Sea veterans cannot boast to have dived. Over the next couple of days, we will move up through St John’s and Fury Shoals, where our guides will find the quietest spots in this vast collection of stunning reef systems, which offer some of the most picturesque and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. Fury Shoals also boasts an amazing selection of marine life, including super-friendly turtles and a resident pod of spinner dolphins. This will bring us up to day six, when, while others cram into local onshore bays, we’ll do a full day and night diving program on some offshore reefs as we travel north. This trip is one of our 21+ itineraries, and should offer around 22 dives on proper safari sites by spending six full nights out of port, returning on the morning of day seven, just before departure time. And, while there are few certainties in life, we’re pretty sure that by taking a different approach, we can give you the best chance of some Southern Solitude.

sections.text: Elphinstone, Daedalus, Fury Shoals Sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals, elegant red gorgonians, vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves, and drop-offs at Elphinstone. Likely oceanic white tip encounters. Mountainous Daedalus with pristine, hard coral formations and a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks. Fury Shoals, a vast reef system to explore, such as Sataya’s resident spinner dolphins, famous swim-throughs and huge porites corals at Sha’ab Claude, mazes and friendly turtles, fantastic coral gardens, and much more that will simply blow you away!

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: This trip offers you some of the best diving in the Red Sea and includes Daedalus, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone. With less distance to travel than some routes, you have more time to dive these iconic sites, and there is less chance of seasickness with shorter sailings and secure moorings. Depending on prevailing weather conditions, your guides will pick sites suitable for night dives outside the Marine Park. Heading first to Fury Shoals, we may dive around the Marsa Alam area or perhaps dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. Oceanic white tips and silky sharks can sometimes be found in the blue, and turtles often visit the south side before heading further south. At Fury Shoals, we have more time to explore the vast reef system than other itineraries afford. Of course, we will dive the classics such as Sha’ab Claude (a.k.a. Claudio) with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals, Malahi with its mazes and friendly turtles, and Abu Galawa Soraya with its fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat smothered with glass fish. Sataya with its resident spinner dolphin population is a must for snorkelling between dives, as well as having some good underwater offerings, and on top of that we can spend time exploring less dived sites such as Sha’ab Hamam (Stairway to Heaven), Abu Galawa Kebir with the Tien Hsing wreck, Gota Sataya and if the weather is kind there are some submerged reefs that can be moored on such as Habili Sameh that will blow you away! Daedalus Reef, part of the Red Sea offshore Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads, especially from May to November, and grey reef sharks. Of course, no trip to the South would be complete without stopping at world-famous Elphinstone, with its sheer walls covered in soft corals, and likely encounters with oceanic white tip sharks. Depending on the experience of the group and the weather, you may even get the chance to dive it at the beginning and end of your amazing trip!

sections.text: lies on the southernmost tip of the Sinai and is one of the best-kept National Parks in Egypt, with waters full of nutrients, steep walls going down to a depth of 1000 meters, attracting a large amount of big fish, and earning itself a reputation as one of the top diving areas in the world. Whilst here, you may have the chance to dive at

sections.text: , a sheer wall falling into the blue, as well as the wreck of the

sections.text: , locally named the ‘Aquarium’, is

sections.heading: Tiran
sections.text: ‘s most popular dive, with the ‘Jackson Drift’ being Sharm’s fastest and most exhilarating drift dive past a stunning wall bursting with prolific coral growth. Occasionally, in the summer months, a school of scalloped hammerheads can be seen.

sections.text: gives you plunging walls covered with soft coral, gorgonian, and colourful fish life. The west wall is darker with overhangs and caves full of glassfish and sweepers. A night dive at

sections.heading: Gordon Reef
sections.text: promises various species of coral, small nudibranchs hidden in the crevices, and soft corals, and a chance to see white tip reef sharks, eagle rays, octopus, and different types of eel, such as moray, peppered, and gold-edged morays. sections.heading: SS Thistlegorm
sections.text: , at Shaab Ali, including a night dive on Thistlegorm. The Thistlegorm was sunk in 1941 after being bombed by the German Luftwaffe while on a mission to deliver a cargo of ammunition and other war materials to the British troops in North Africa.

sections.heading: Safaga, Brothers & Elphinstone:
sections.text: Panorama Reef, Middle Reef, Salem Express, Brother Islands, Abu Dabab, Elphinstone Sheer walls draped in colourful soft corals and gorgonian forests at the Brothers and Elphinstone. sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: The area around Safaga has some great diving, the best being the offshore reefs of Panorama Reef, Middle Reef, and Abu Kafan. Some divers say this area equals the great sites of Ras Mohamed. The diving offers a combination of shallow reef dives and drop-offs, as well as the famous wreck of the Salem Express. The Salem Express is a dramatic wreck dive. It is now home to a thriving underwater life, including a famous resident frogfish, blue-spotted stingrays, angel and butterfly fish. The ship itself is covered in a large quantity of hard and soft corals. It is one of the largest wrecks in the Egyptian Red Sea, roughly the same size as the Thistlegorm. There is superb wall diving at Panorama: on the south-east side of the plateau is a gorgonian and glassfish corner, with the whole plateau covered in soft corals, and on the south side is an anemone city. Hal Hal (Middle Reef) is a rarely chosen dive site due to its distance from the coast, which makes it a virgin spot. The north side is a drop off going down to 80 metres and is a perfect location to spot tunas, barracudas, turtles and sharks. The southern side has colourful coral gardens along with some caves and canyons. Abu Kafan is a 300-metre-long, narrow reef offering a plateau at both north and south tips. We normally jump in the water on the north plateau and glide with the frequent strong current southwards along the impressive walls covered with soft and black coral, giant fans and gorgonians. The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Large tuna, jacks, and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silvertips, silky and oceanic white tip sharks, and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can be found here. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother. Abu Dabab is six reefs commonly known as “Father's Steps” or “Fathers Stepping Stones” and as the name suggests, a set of fairly shallow reefs ranging from depths of 25 metres to the seafloor. In between Abu Dabab II and III, at approximately 15 metres, is the wreckage of a small ship sunk after a fire in 2004. Elphinstone is approximately 30km from Port Ghalib; Elphinstone reef is 300 metres long with sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals and elegant red gorgonians descending to around 40 metres. Other areas of the reef have near-vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves, and drop-offs of up to 100 metres. Elphinstone is known to experience some strong currents, attracting many diverse species such as barracuda, angel fish, groupers, Napoleons, morays, reef sharks, and great shoals of dogtooth tuna and jacks. Occasional sightings include dolphins, turtles, oceanic white tip, and hammerhead sharks.

sections.heading: Itinerary Highlights
sections.text: Spoilt for choice with 21+ DIVES at the most remote and rewarding reef systems of the south A less arduous itinerary for a more relaxed diving pace Stunning typography with coral gardens, walls, overhangs, and swim-throughs Expect to see turtles, sharks, grey reef sharks, reef fishes, macro, shoals of glass fish, snappers, butterfly fish, and barracuda This trip takes you to some of the best diving the Red Sea has to offer. Here, diving is less arduous, so it’s a trip for those who want to see the best but have a more relaxed time while doing so. As a 21+ DIVES cruise, there’s a good chance to enjoy 21 or more dives on a 7-day safari if you choose to. Sailing to the southernmost reefs, you’ll depart from Port Ghalib and dive some sites to the South before sailing overnight to your southernmost point in the St. John’s area. Depending on weather, government approval, and marine life sightings in recent weeks, we may sail to the southernmost islands of Rocky and Zabargad, or we’ll moor instead in the vast reef system of St John’s to begin the adventure in the South. When leaving Port Ghalib, the route can sometimes dive Abu Dabab on the first or last day. Often spoilt for choice, your guides will pick sites that they know to be the best for the time of year and can find excellent alternatives should the weather affect the normal route. Although the distances are long, where possible, we travel overnight, so, as a 21-plus route, we aim to get as many dives in as possible at some of the most impressive reefs. Below are some of the highlights. On the way to Fury Shoals, we’ll dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. At Fury Shoals, dive Sha’ab Claude with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals. White tip reef sharks and an anemone, and a clownfish settlement can be seen a little off the reef to the South. Abu Galawa Soraya has a fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat populated with glass fish. St John's is a vast collection of small reefs offering some of the most remote and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. This incredibly beautiful reef lies a short distance north of the Sudanese border. The reef covers a huge area, and many dives would be needed to explore the numerous coral heads and islands. Habili Ali offers giant gorgonians and black corals, whilst grey reef, silvertip, and schools of hammerhead sharks might be found on the west side. Habili Gafaar is a mass of soft corals teaming with shoals of snappers, butterfly fish, and barracudas. Mantas, grey ree, and silvertip sharks can often be seen in the blue. Gota Kebir is a massive reef, famous for its tunnels and south plateau, where jacks and barracudas can be seen, and the occasional manta. The tunnels are ideal for novice cave divers. Gota Soraya is rated as possibly one of the best wall dives in the Red Sea, with overhangs and cracks in the reef wall full of glass fish and sweepers and an abundance of corals, Grey Reef, Silvertips, and Hammerhead sharks. On the last day as we head back to port, we will try to take in a dive or two on the world famous Elphinstone Reef if weather and diver experience permits us, or we will finish in the Abu Dabab area perhaps with another dive or two closer to Port Ghalib to relax and unwind before your final night in port. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator.

sections.heading: Southern Solitude:
sections.text: Elphinstone, Daedalus, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, Abu Dabab Going ‘against the flow’ to see the best sites in the southern Red Sea at their quietest times. Elphinstone, Daedalus, and St John’s at their quietest, with the rarely-dived sites of Rocky and Zabargad also included. This is a 21+ itinerary with all dives made offshore. By staying out of port on the last night, there’s potential for up to 22 dives on the trip – the most any of our itineraries offer. A diverse range of marine life, such as tuna, barracudas, jacks, groupers, Napoleon, bumphead parrotfish, and sharks, including hammerheads and occasionally silky and oceanic white tips. Dolphins and turtles in the Fury Shoals, while manta, thresher sharks, and whalesharks can always surprise. This fantastic itinerary gives divers the wonderful opportunity to ‘go against the flow’ and dive the best sites of the Red Sea on what should be their quietest days. By approaching these iconic sites in the opposite direction to most standard itineraries, we hope to offer you the best chance to dive with the fewest number of people around you.

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: Southern Solitude is a dive-focused trip, heading out of Port Ghalib and immediately arriving in the Elphinstone area. This enables us to make a check dive nearby and then get straight to a site which is normally frequented on the final days of trips. With fewer boats around, it should give the chance to enjoy the 300-metre-long reef’s colourful pink and red soft coral sheer walls in relative peace and quiet. We’ll then go to Daedalus, arriving before most others, to take in its deep walls and drop-offs, which offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found, before heading down to the exceptionally remote, and usually quiet, Rocky and Zabargad Islands, where even many Red Sea veterans cannot boast to have dived. Over the next couple of days, we will move up through St John’s and Fury Shoals, where our guides will find the quietest spots in this vast collection of stunning reef systems, which offer some of the most picturesque and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. Fury Shoals also boasts an amazing selection of marine life, including super-friendly turtles and a resident pod of spinner dolphins. This will bring us up to day six, when, while others cram into local onshore bays, we’ll do a full day and night diving program on some offshore reefs as we travel north. This trip is one of our 21+ itineraries, and should offer around 22 dives on proper safari sites by spending six full nights out of port, returning on the morning of day seven, just before departure time. And, while there are few certainties in life, we’re pretty sure that by taking a different approach, we can give you the best chance of some Southern Solitude.

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: Starting from Hurghada, we sail north towards Gubal Island and on to Abu Nuhas and its four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the ‘Lentil Wreck’ and the ‘Tile Wreck’, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life. Explore the Rosalie Moller (the sister ship of the slightly more famous Thistlegorm), which lies from 30 to 50 metres deep and is in excellent condition. Although the visibility is not always good, the wreck is covered in glassfish from bow to stern, and hunting them are masses of lionfish. Around the wreck are the usual pelagics such as tuna, trevallies, Emperor fis,h and many more. A short ride across the Straits of Gubal and you visit the most famous wreck of the Red Sea, the SS Thistlegorm! An awe-inspiring World War II British vessel with a cargo full of armaments, Bedford trucks, and BSA motorbikes, which were all destined for the British troops in North Africa. She was sunk by the German Luftwaffe and now lies in 30 metres of water. Depending on divers’ experience, along with weather and current conditions, we try to offer a night dive here. Nearby is the Ras Mohamed National Park, offering a morning dive at the renowned ‘Shark and Yolanda’ reefs. Ras Mohamed National Park is the furthest Sinai destination before heading south towards the Brothers. The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore from El Quseir. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Big tuna, barracudas, jack,s and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can sometimes be found there. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother. For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks. The boat will then sail back to Hurghada via Safaga, where you can dive at Panorama Reef or the famous wreck of Salem Express for a memorable finale!

sections.heading: Get Wrecked:
sections.text: Abu Nuhas, Straits of Gubal, Ulysses, Rosalie Moller, Thistlegorm, Dunraven, and others 21+ DIVES cruise Dive the “best of the best” iconic wrecks the north Red Sea has to offer. Explore the wreck graveyard at Abu Nuhas; Carnatic, Chrisoula K, Kimon M, and Giannis D The infamous wreck of SS Thistlegorm and sister Rosalie Moller Dunraven at Ras Mohamed, Ulysses, and so much more The Get Wrecked cruise combines the ‘best of the best’ of the most famous wrecks in the northern Red Sea, along with some stunning reef diving. As a 21+ DIVES cruise, there’s a good chance to enjoy 21 or more dives on a 7-day safari if you choose to.

sections.heading: Day 2-6:
sections.text: El Mina, an Egyptian mine sweeper lying just outside Hurghada’s harbour; the Carnatic, the Chrisoula K (’tile wreck’), the Kimon M (‘lentil wreck’) and Giannis D at Abu Nuhas; at Gubal islands we dive the Barge, the Ulysses (sunk in 1887) and the Rosalie Moeller; next onto the Kingston (or Sarah H, sunk in 1881) lying at Shag Rock; and, of course, the Dunraven (sunk 1876) at Beacon Rock situated in the Ras Mohammed National Park, then finally the most famous wreck in the Red Sea, the Thistlegorm, which lies at Shaab Ali. These wrecks are spectacular and make fantastic material for the underwater photographer, being smothered in corals, especially the Carnatic, which sank in 1869. The famous SS Thistlegorm and the Rosalie Moller are World War II wrecks and one of the highlights of this cruise. The SS Thistlegorm was sunk in 1941 after being bombed by the German Luftwaffe while on a mission to deliver a cargo of ammunition and other war materials to the British troops in North Africa. The Rosalie Moeller, carrying a cargo of coal, suffered the same fate just two days later. In between wreck dives, you will also visit the reefs of the Straits of Gubal, the Gulf of Suez, and those to the north of Hurghada. A variety of deep walls and hard coral gardens with an abundance of reef fish make them well worth a visit. Diving wrecks is subject to the diver’s experience. Please be aware that the dive sites and areas mentioned in our itineraries are not guaranteed. sections.heading: Itinerary Highlights
sections.text: Spoilt for choice with 21+ DIVES at the most remote and rewarding reef systems of the south A less arduous itinerary for a more relaxed diving pace Stunning typography with coral gardens, walls, overhangs, and swim-throughs Expect to see turtles, sharks, grey reef sharks, reef fishes, macro, shoals of glass fish, snappers, butterfly fish, and barracuda This trip takes you to some of the best diving the Red Sea has to offer. Here, diving is less arduous, so it’s a trip for those who want to see the best but have a more relaxed time while doing so. As a 21+ DIVES cruise, there’s a good chance to enjoy 21 or more dives on a 7-day safari if you choose to. Sailing to the southernmost reefs, you’ll depart from Port Ghalib and dive some sites to the South before sailing overnight to your southernmost point in the St. John’s area. Depending on weather, government approval, and marine life sightings in recent weeks, we may sail to the southernmost islands of Rocky and Zabargad, or we’ll moor instead in the vast reef system of St John’s to begin the adventure in the South. When leaving Port Ghalib, the route can sometimes dive Abu Dabab on the first or last day. Often spoilt for choice, your guides will pick sites that they know to be the best for the time of year and can find excellent alternatives should the weather affect the normal route. Although the distances are long, where possible, we travel overnight, so, as a 21-plus route, we aim to get as many dives in as possible at some of the most impressive reefs. Below are some of the highlights. On the way to Fury Shoals, we’ll dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. At Fury Shoals, dive Sha’ab Claude with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals. White tip reef sharks and an anemone, and a clownfish settlement can be seen a little off the reef to the South. Abu Galawa Soraya has a fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat populated with glass fish. St John's is a vast collection of small reefs offering some of the most remote and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. This incredibly beautiful reef lies a short distance north of the Sudanese border. The reef covers a huge area, and many dives would be needed to explore the numerous coral heads and islands. Habili Ali offers giant gorgonians and black corals, whilst grey reef, silvertip, and schools of hammerhead sharks might be found on the west side. Habili Gafaar is a mass of soft corals teaming with shoals of snappers, butterfly fish, and barracudas. Mantas, grey ree, and silvertip sharks can often be seen in the blue. Gota Kebir is a massive reef, famous for its tunnels and south plateau, where jacks and barracudas can be seen, and the occasional manta. The tunnels are ideal for novice cave divers. Gota Soraya is rated as possibly one of the best wall dives in the Red Sea, with overhangs and cracks in the reef wall full of glass fish and sweepers and an abundance of corals, Grey Reef, Silvertips, and Hammerhead sharks. On the last day as we head back to port, we will try to take in a dive or two on the world famous Elphinstone Reef if weather and diver experience permits us, or we will finish in the Abu Dabab area perhaps with another dive or two closer to Port Ghalib to relax and unwind before your final night in port. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator.

sections.heading: Day 1:
sections.text: Afternoon/Evening Transfer to Travco for embarkation. Upon arrival, you'll be welcomed on board, followed by check-in, cabin arrangements, and a boat briefing. Port authority permissions will be finalized, and the boat will depart early the following morning.

sections.heading: Days 2 - 7:
sections.text: Start your morning with a sail to a nearby temple or Ras Katy for a check dive. Then, head into the Gulf of Suez, passing Yolanda Reef, named after a 74-meter-long Cypriot freighter that struck the reef on April 1, 1980. While most of the ship has since fallen over the drop-off, remnants of its cargo, including bathtubs, toilets, and bathroom fittings, remain scattered for divers to explore. Continue to the historic wreck of Dunraven , a 125-year-old vessel largely intact, covered in vibrant corals, and teeming with marine life. One of the most famous Red Sea wrecks, the Thistlegorm , lies upright on the seabed at 33 meters. This impressive 127-meter-long wreck gained fame after Jacques Cousteau dived it in 1956, though its location remained a mystery until rediscovered in 1992. Nearby, the 78-meter-long Kingston wreck, dating back to 1881, rests at the northern edge of Shag Rock. Crossing the Gulf of Suez, you’ll reach Abu Nuhas, a haven for wreck enthusiasts. Here, you’ll find the legendary wrecks of the Giannis D , Carnatic , Chrisoula K , and Kimon M , lying along the northern side of a reef with a sandy seafloor and steep coral slopes. The reef, named after the Arabic word for copper ( Nuhas ), is both historically and visually captivating. At Gubal Island, discover the Barge wreck, a site rich in soft corals and marine life during the day and transformed into a spectacular night dive. Weather permitting, you may also explore the deeper wrecks of the Ulysses or the Rosalie Moller . Just two days after the Thistlegorm sank, the Rosalie Moller met the same fate and now lies upright at depth, making it a challenging dive for experienced divers due to strong currents and limited visibility. In between wreck dives, you'll visit breathtaking coral reefs at Sha’ab Mahmoud and Ras Mohamed National Park, showcasing the Red Sea’s diverse underwater beauty.

ghazala-explorer::Daedalus, Rocky & St J.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.
ghazala-explorer::Daedalus, Rocky & St J.intro: This 8-day liveaboard takes you to the best of Egypt's Deep South, venturing far offshore to some of the Red Sea's most thrilling and remote dive sites. From the shark-patrolled waters of Daedalus Reef to the dramatic walls of Rocky Island and Zabargad, and the pristine coral gardens of the St. Johns reef system, every dive promises an unforgettable encounter. With up to 4 dives per day, including night dives, this route is designed for divers seeking big pelagics, vibrant reefs, and a true deep south adventure — all departing and returning from Hurghada

sections.heading: Day 1:
sections.text: Embark in Hurghada and settle into your cabin. Safety/check dive in the afternoon. Welcome dinner on board.

sections.heading: Days 2–7:
sections.text: 3 to 4 dives per day, including a night dive where conditions allow. 2 dives scheduled on crossing days.

sections.heading: A typical day on board:
sections.text: Early light breakfast before the morning dive. Morning dive followed by a full breakfast. Second dive mid-morning. Lunch on board. Third dive in the afternoon, with a fourth dive where possible. Night dive (where conditions and site permit). Dinner on board.

sections.heading: Daedalus Reef
sections.text: — Remote offshore reef famous for oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and large pelagic encounters.

sections.heading: Rocky Island & Zabargad
sections.text: — Dramatic walls and pinnacles teeming with sharks, barracuda, and vibrant coral life.

sections.heading: St. Johns Reef System
sections.text: — One of Egypt's most pristine reef systems, featuring spectacular coral gardens, diverse marine life, and stunning underwater topography.

sections.heading: Day 8:
sections.text: Final morning dive. Sail back to Hurghada. Disembark and farewell.

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: The dive sites on this route are renowned for some of the Red Sea's most spectacular marine encounters. Daedalus Reef is famous for its resident oceanic whitetip sharks and passing hammerheads, while large schools of barracuda and trevally patrol the open blue. Rocky Island and Zabargad offer dramatic walls alive with anthias, groupers, and reef sharks cruising the current-swept pinnacles. The St. Johns reef system is home to some of the healthiest and most colorful coral gardens in the Red Sea, sheltering turtles, moray eels, napoleon wrasse, and an abundance of reef fish. Night dives reveal a completely different world, with hunting lionfish, octopus, and cuttlefish emerging after dark. The last dive will be on the final day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

Exceptional visibility at St. Johns to experience the common shark and pelagic action there.

golden-dolphin-iv::10 days: North - SS T.name: 10 days: North - SS Turkia - Ras Mohamed - Dahab (Hurghada - Hurghada)
golden-dolphin-iv::10 days: North - SS T.experience: Advanced Open Water - 30 minimum logged dives required.
golden-dolphin-iv::10 days: North - SS T.intro: The SS Turkia was built by Earles Shipbuilding and Engineering Co. in Hall (England) in 1909. The steam cargo ship named Livorno, with a length of 91m, a width of 13m, and 1671 tons, was used for a variety of trade routes in England and Northern Europe. Between 1920 and 1935, the ship was sold to Greece, and they named it SS Turkia. In May 1941, the SS Turkia was on its way from New York to Piräus. The government cargo included explosives, gyres, coils of wire, ingots, vehicles, and firearms. Close to the Channel of Suez, it sank due to two different stories: fire on board and/or being hit by a bomb. At a depth between 10m and 24m, full of soft and hard corals, it is a great experience for divers to discover the Wreck from outside and inside. The SS Thistlegorm is probably the most famous wreck in the Red Sea. The British cargo ship was on its way to bring military equipment of all kinds for the British troops in North Africa. But then, on the 6th of October 1941, a German bomber attacked the Thistlegorm. The wreck is lying upright on the sea bottom at 32m. Especially interesting is the cargo: Tanks, trucks, motorcycles, weapons, a railway carriage, and two railway engines. Starting from the North on the Eastern side of the Sinai Peninsula are the Straits of Tiran, also one of the most famous diving areas in the Red Sea. Situated in the middle of the straits are four coral reefs: Gordon, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Jackson Reef. The Gordon Reef is marked by the wreck of a large commercial freighter. The reef composition is quite varied, with patchy sections, sand beds, and full-fledged coral gardens. In the center of the reef slope, a shark amphitheater or bowl dips to 24m; with luck, a variety of shark species can be seen sleeping on the sandy bottom. The site boasts a very good range of corals, with lots of branching varieties. All of the corals are well preserved, in densely grown patches that often show a remarkable mix of different species. Fish life is not the most profuse in the Straits of Tiran, but there are some notable surprises, including a huge moray eel with a body as thick as a small diver's waist. Trigger fish abound while surgeons and jacks swim in moderately large schools, and angels, parrot fish, and small wrasse are all present in good numbers. Large Napoleon's wrasse can often be seen along the reef. The Thomas Reef includes some plateau sections and a very deep canyon running along the reef’s southern section. It is the smallest of the four Tiran reefs. The reef’s upper section is a riot of color, encompassing some of the finest soft coral growth in the Sinai region. Huge, densely packed fields of Dendronephthya of every imaginable hue are spread across the reef, along with antler corals, fine Stylophora, some Acropora, and many other stony coral forms. Fish life is also rich, with the greatest concentration in the shallows. Lyretail cod and other groupers grow to great size, and wide varieties of rabbit fish and wrasse congregate along the reef face, accompanied by box and puffer fish. The only reason to go deeper than 20m at Thomas Reef is to explore the canyon. The Woodhouse Reef is a long, narrow reef running at an angle from northeast to southwest. Woodhouse is generally divided into a drift along the reef’s eastern side. Coral cover is excellent throughout the reef, with dense growth all over; there are a few sandy patches at depths of around 20m. Many species are present, but because of the sheltered position of the reef, away from the main current, a certain amount of sedimentation has affected the corals here. Pelagic fish, including big tuna and schools of jacks, fusiliers, snapper, surgeons, and unicorns, also school here, along with thousands of other reef fish. On the northern edge of the Jackson Reef, the wreck of a grounded freighter stands as a warning to the shipping in the busy straits; most of its hull has been salvaged for scrap, leaving only a skeletal hulk. The steep-sided walls of Jackson Reef are among the finest in the Sinai region; the current-swept reef is densely grown with a real profusion of hard and soft corals, with special accents provided by luxuriant gorgonian fans, sea whips, and black corals, and vivid growths of soft coral. Fish life, not surprisingly, is excellent. The strong current brings plenty of nutrients for the reef and schooling fish; current and profile combine to tempt pelagic fish in from the open water, and large schools of barracuda and jacks are common here, as are larger predators, including several species of shark. The smaller reef species on which these pelagic visitors feed are profuse. Midway between Sharm el-Sheik and Aqaba is Dahab, on a narrow stretch of coast, but at the same time at the deepest and widest point in the Gulf. The reefs are mostly shallow down to about 20-30m, e.g., B. at Southern Oasis or the northern canyon. The canyon is not for everyone, though, as it features a deep fissure that starts at around 15m and has the deepest exit at around 50m. In between, there are only a few exit possibilities, so the dive goes in the direction of cave diving and must be planned. Exceptional fish can already be found in shallow water, sand, and scree up to a depth of around 10m, e.g., the well camouflaged Red Sea Walkman. The devil fish is one of the poisonous stone fish, so beware, dangerous. The harmless pygmy winged fishes, which are up to 8 cm in size, live in the 5-meter range, and they too are extremely difficult to spot. You can even reach excellent coral gardens in Dahab: in the north, the national park is called Abu Galum, in the south, Gabr al Bint is known for its hard corals and its groupers. But one place has made Dahab world famous: the Blue Hole. It is about 10 km north of the city and is a dark blue hole about 50-70 m in diameter and 120 m deep. Outside of the Blue Hole, however, the steep face is beautifully overgrown, and occasionally even large fish can be found. This drop-off can be reached through a reef crevice at a depth of about 7 m. The next breakthrough is only at 56m, again with a 26m long and a few meters wide arch, i.e., beyond our spot diver limit and only reserved for the Tekkies with their special gas mixtures.

golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.name: Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elphinstone (Hurghada - Hurghada)
golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.
golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.intro: The Brother Islands are one of the best diving spots in the world. The islands – the Big Brother and the Little Brother – are two small exposed promontories that rise out of the water in the middle of the sea, about 60 km from the Egyptian coastline. The Little Brother has a very high concentration of marine life in a relatively small area. The walls are literally covered with sponges, anemones, and all sorts of hard and soft corals in an astonishing variety of colors and shapes. Of course, you will find plenty of fish here. It is not unusual to see sharks, including hammerheads, thresher sharks, grey reef sharks, silvertip, and white-tip reef sharks. About one kilometer north of the Little Brother lies the Big Brother. Situated in the middle of the island is a lighthouse. When it is not too windy, you can dive the wreck NUMIDIA, which rests on the reef on the northern side of the island at depths between 5 m and 80 m. This 150 m long ship sank in 1901 and is now completely covered with both hard and soft corals and gorgonias. On the northwest side of the island, you will find another wreck: the AIDA. This 82 m long steamship sank in 1957. The remaining pieces of the wreck are scattered across the reef, and just the backside of the hull can be found between 34 m and 60 m. It is nicely overgrown and well worth a visit. Because of strong currents and potentially high waves, diving at the Brother Islands is not easy. This safari is recommended only for experienced divers. The Daedalus Reef is a huge reef formation located about 180 km south of the Brother Islands. The reef is surrounded by sheer walls all around, featuring a plateau on its southern side that slopes from 28 m beside the reef to 40 m at the edge of the drop-off. If the weather is good, try to drift along one of the sides of the reef. Reef and hammerhead sharks are often spotted here. Underwater marine life is more abundant than anywhere else, with schools of surgeonfish, fusiliers, and carangids. The reef of Elphinstone, a truly legendary site, is one of the most beautiful reefs in the Red Sea. Its north and south plateaus and walls are covered in soft corals, black corals, wire corals, and gorgonias. Hammerheads, oceanic whitetip sharks, and grey reef sharks can also be spotted here.

Daedalus Reef offers a high chance to see schooling hammerheads and occasional manta rays, while Elphinstone is known for its stunning coral walls and sightings of oceanic whitetips and grey reef sharks. Rich coral gardens, anthias clouds, and diverse reef life make every dive vibrant and exciting. This itinerary is ideal for experienced divers seeking big fish action and pristine reefscapes. golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.intro: The Brother Islands are one of the best diving spots in the world. The islands – the Big Brother and the Little Brother – are two small exposed promontories that rise out of the water in the middle of the sea, about 60 km from the Egyptian coastline. The Little Brother has a very high concentration of marine life in a relatively small area. The walls are literally covered with sponges, anemones, and all sorts of hard and soft corals in an astonishing variety of colors and shapes. Of course, you will find plenty of fish here. It is not unusual to see sharks, including hammerheads, thresher sharks, grey reef sharks, silvertip, and white-tip reef sharks. About one kilometer north of the Little Brother lies the Big Brother. Situated in the middle of the island is a lighthouse. When it is not too windy, you can dive the wreck NUMIDIA, which rests on the reef on the northern side of the island at depths between 5 m and 80 m. This 150 m long ship sank in 1901 and is now completely covered with both hard and soft corals and gorgonias. On the northwest side of the island, you will find another wreck: the AIDA. This 82 m long steamship sank in 1957. The remaining pieces of the wreck are scattered across the reef, and just the backside of the hull can be found between 34 m and 60 m. golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.
golden-dolphin-iv::Brother Islands - Dae.intro: The Brother Islands are undoubtedly among the world's best dive sites. Rising steeply from great depths, two small islands, Big Brother and Little Brother, lie isolated in the Red Sea, about 60 km off the coast. Daedalus Reef is surrounded by a sloping wall and features a plateau on its southern side, dropping from 30 m at the wall to 40 m at the edge. The plateau is covered in colorful marine life, extending into the shallows. Turtles and numerous schools of fish frequent this area. A closer look reveals nudibranchs, scorpionfish, and stonefish. Thresher sharks are also frequently spotted at the plateau. Rocky Island is a legendary dive site that makes every diver's heart beat faster. The fringing reef surrounding this bird-nesting island promotes the growth of all kinds of marine life. The former sapphire-mining island of Zabargad is a dive site distinguished by its remarkable diversity. Here, divers can explore steep walls, glide over drop-offs, experience the thrill of open water at the edges of the drop-offs, circumnavigate coral towers, and explore inlets in the sheltered shallows, observe fish, or simply admire this unique coral garden as they swim by. Deep, far to the south (at the latitude of Rocky Island), lie the St. Johns Reefs. This reef group offers divers a virtually untouched underwater world. A few hours south of St. Johns, the approximately 6-kilometer-long Abu Fandera reef chain stretches from west to east. Between the six elongated reefs are so-called passages, which are wonderfully diveable channels with varying topographies. Dozens of ergs (reef blocks) at depths of 15 to 20 meters, covered in beautiful soft corals, awaken the spirit of exploration. Although Elphinstone Reef has become very popular with divers in recent years due to its proximity to the coast, it is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful reefs in Egypt and a "must-see" for every diver. Not very wide but long, a plateau extends in stages from 18 to 55 meters in the north. Safaga, with its fantastic dive sites, Abu Kifan and Panorama Reef, is, along with diving on the Salem Express, a successful part of this safari.

The Red Sea is one of the world's most fascinating diving destinations and is home to a unique underwater world.
