red-sea-blue-force-2::Extended North (Sh.experience: Open Water - 30 minimum logged dives required.
red-sea-blue-force-2::Extended North (Sh.intro: The EXTENDED NORTH Route is the most complete route in the North of the Red Sea and It is considered the best route to discover Red Sea diving. It is a very complete and simple route for diving, matching all diving levels, although we recommend advanced open water level or equivalent. The sailing on this route is very short and pleasant, reaching the furthest dive sites in about two hours. The wide range of dive sites will give you the opportunity to diving amazing reefs like those found in Ras Mohammed National Park and the Straits of Tiran, visit a living WWII museum at the wreck of SS Thistlegorm and enjoy all the underwater wonders of the Red Sea reefs in pristine dive sites like Small Crack or Shag Rock and the possibility of snorkeling with dolphins. On this route, we offer 7 days liveaboard with 6 full days of diving. The last day is to desaturate nitrogen and do a bit of shopping and clubbing in Sharm el-sheik. TRAVEL PROGRAM “EXTENDED NORTH ROUTE”

sections.heading: Saturday:
sections.text: SHARM EL SHEIKH – LIVEABOARD DIVING CRUISE Meet & Assistance at the airport in Sharm El Sheikh by our staff at the airport. Transfer to the jetty. Embarking from 19:00 pm onwards. Welcome cocktail, boat, and crew introduction. Cabins distribution. Dinner on board.

sections.heading: Sunday to Friday:
sections.text: LIVEABOARD DIVING CRUISE “NORTH ROUTE” Liveaboard diving cruise on full board basis (including water) and 6 days diving, up to 4 dives per day. Some of the highlights of the route are the Straits of Tiran, the National Park of Ras Mohamed, and wrecks like Thistlegorm.

sections.heading: Saturday:
sections.text: Port of disembarkation – SHARM EL SHEIKH Disembarkation in Sharm el-sheik. Transfer to Sharm el-sheik by road, lunch non-included. 5* Hotel accommodation. Leisure time to enjoy the local environment and do some shopping. Dinner at the hotel.

sections.heading: Sunday:
sections.text: SHARM EL SHEIKH Breakfast. Airport transfer. Check-out formalities assisted by our staff.

sections.heading: STRAIT OF TIRAN
sections.text: The Strait of Tiran is actually a submerged ridge that rises from more than 300 meters depth and extends from the southeast point of Sinai until the island of Tiran. It is basically a passage between the Gulf of Aqaba and the main basin of the Red Sea, forming an area of strong tidal currents. In the Strait, we find 4 reefs that are famous for the quality of their coral and abundant sea life. Large oceanic fauna sightings are typical.

sections.heading: ANEMONE CITY, SHARK REEF & YOLANDA REEF
sections.text: The most famous dive in the Red Sea and considered one of the best sites in the world. We start off at Anemone City, where dozens of huge anemones (Magnificent heteractis) hosting a multitude of clownfish and damsels are to be found. From here we leap into the blue, crossing over the depths below, to the walls of shark reef. Along the way, possible sightings include; sharks, tuna, red snapper, and other large pelagic marine animals. From there, the dive continues on to shallower water between the two reefs. Here, you’ll be able to see parts of the freighter ship: Yolanda, which struck the reef and gave it its name. Among the debris, you’ll find a large collection of toilets and the remains of the captain’s BMW. The area around the wreck often houses lionfish, blue-spotted stingrays, and moray eels. The entire stretch between the two reefs is strewn with rocks overgrown with coral, as well as lots of coral on the sides of the reef, which contrast nicely with the white, sandy bottom. The shallow water, the light reflecting off from the bottom, and colorful reefs make this a photographer’s paradise.

sections.heading: JACKFISH ALLEY
sections.text: The traditional dive starts off with a cave at 5 meters which is actually a swim through coming out at a depth of 9 meters. The cave is covered with small gorgonian fans and a crack on the roof allows the rays of sun through. From here we swim on to a long Sandy Alley that gives the name to this site; it was originally named Fisherman's Bank, due to a large amount of jackfish found here. You can see barracuda, tuna, and all the usual Red Sea residents here. The dive finishes at the end of the sandy alley where most people are on 50 bar.

sections.heading: RAS GHOZLANI
sections.text: Ras Ghozlani is a beautiful dive site with lots of interesting things to see and discover. You start off on a sandy slope at a depth of around 6 meters which slowly descends to the drop-off found at around 25 meters. Tons of pinnacles in different shapes and sizes distract us with their fauna and coral during the whole dive. The pinnacles are covered with Table corals, big Gorgonian fans, and healthy soft corals in many different colors. The pinnacles are teeming Anthias and other colorful reef fish. Embark from 19.00 pm. Disembarkation maximum at 10.00 am . Passengers holding EU nationality need to have their passport valid for at least six months since their arrival to Egypt. Other nationalities check with Consulate/Embassy representative's conditions of entry in Egypt.

red-sea-explorer::Brother Islands, Daeda.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.

sections.heading: Brothers:
sections.text: Sharks, wrecks, and drop-offs – there is almost nothing that does not exist here. The well-known thresher shark cleaning station on Little Brother, grey reef sharks, hammerheads, and Longimanus guarantee exciting dives. The spectacular drop-offs are covered with soft corals, as well as the two wrecks, Numidia and Aida, at Big Brother.

sections.heading: Daedalus:
sections.text: The large reef lies south of the Brothers and is notable for its intact hard coral gardens and the popular anemone city. However, Daedalus has become famous for its legendary hammerhead schools, which guarantee exciting dives.

sections.heading: Elphinstone:
sections.text: The reef is known for its two plateaus on the north and south sides, with good chances of hammerhead encounters. A frequent visitor is the curious oceanic whitetip shark (Longimanus). Fantastic corals, Napoleon wrasses, and turtles make the trip to Elphinstone Reef the perfect ending of the tour.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: The crew will transfer guests from the airport or hotel to the ship. A welcome briefing, cabin allocation, and ship orientation will take place before embarking. Guests can familiarize themselves with the vessel, set up their equipment, and get comfortable. General dive procedures and safety briefings will also be provided to prepare for the trip.

sections.heading: Day 2–6
sections.text: Guests can enjoy up to 3–4 scheduled dives per day, depending on the itinerary and sea conditions. Night dives may be offered when conditions and local regulations allow; however, they may be restricted or not possible on certain routes (e.g., offshore or Marine Park itineraries such as BDE). Each dive is preceded by a detailed briefing to ensure all divers are well-prepared. There are typically two experienced dive guides on board, maintaining a maximum ratio of 8 divers per guide, ensuring a safe and personalized diving experience.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: The final day of diving includes 2–3 scheduled dives, depending on the itinerary and timing, followed by sailing back to the harbor.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: After breakfast and check-out, preparations for disembarkation begin. The crew will say goodbye to guests and arrange transfers to the airport, assisting with check-in for onward flights.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: Oceanic whitetip sharks, scalloped hammerhead sharks, thresher sharks, grey reef sharks, manta rays, dolphins, barracuda, giant trevally, tuna, Napoleon wrasse, giant moray eels, anthias, fusiliers, butterflyfish, octopus, nudibranchs, and cleaner shrimp. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. sections.heading: Fury Shoals/Shaab Claudio:
sections.text: Diving is very relaxed here because of the shallow depth and little current. A small cave system that is very easy to dive in, attracting great light effects, and is ideal for photographers. A beautiful Sha’ab Sataya is also known as “Dolphin House” and is located in the south of the Fury Shoals. The horseshoe-shaped reef includes a large lagoon where dolphins can be encountered quite often. Especially when snorkelling, there is the opportunity to experience unforgettable moments with the playful marine mammals. The reef is also great for night dives.

sections.heading: Zabargad:
sections.text: Zabargad Island is around 3.5 km long with many interesting dive sites. A nameless wreck with a length of 70 m lies between 1 and 24 meters on the sandy bottom. At low tide, the mast towers over the water. It is possible to explore the bridge and the engine room. A hard coral garden on the west side and a colorful plateau in the south offer a great variety.

sections.heading: Rocky Island:
sections.text: Rocky Island is a tiny island near Zabargad. The legendary dive site is surrounded by a large fringing reef that seems to drop steeply to infinity. The reef is swarming with life and covered with lots of gorgonians, soft and fan corals. With a bit of luck, you can also spot big fish like grey reef sharks, white-tip sharks, and dolphins.

sections.heading: SS. Thistlegorm:
sections.text: One of the most famous and popular wrecks in the Red Sea is certainly the SS Thistlegorm. Rediscovered in 1956 by Jacques Cousteau, the wreck offers one-of-a-kind dives with a variety of marine life and spectacular holds with relics of the Second World War. While diving, you can discover trucks and motorcycles. Worth seeing is the stern with its machine guns and the locomotive on the ocean floor next to the wreck. Watch out for ammunition lying around!

sections.heading: Abu Nuhas:
sections.text: Abu Nuhas ship graveyard on the Gubal Strait houses four wrecks at moderate depths. The Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M are overgrown with colourful corals and form artificial reefs for numerous fish, shrimp, octopus, and moray eels. Interesting dives are guaranteed, because each of the wrecks is different.

sections.heading: Strait of Tiran:
sections.text: The popular reefs of the Strait of Tiran, Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, and Gordon Reef, promise diversified dives. At Jackson Riff, life is buzzing with turtles, anthias, and numerous fusiliers. The wonderful soft corals enchant every diver. With a bit of luck, hammerhead sharks can be seen at the outer part of the reef or at Gordon Reef. Woodhouse and Gordon offer steep walls, the famous Thomas Canyon, and beautiful gorgonians.

sections.heading: Ras Mohamed (Shark & Yolanda):
sections.text: The dive site is located on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula and promises a variety of highlights for divers. The bottomless wall at Shark Reef is beautifully overgrown with soft corals. Especially in the summer months, the reef hosts plenty of fish. Schools of snappers, jacks, and batfish are gathering in the deep blue at the drop-off. With a little luck, grey reef sharks and barracudas can be seen. Yolanda Reef is named after the sunken cargo ship. The ship itself has slipped to great depths, its cargo is still scattered on the reef between colourful corals: toilets, bathtubs, and even the leftovers of a car are among the attractions.

sections.text: The diversified dive sites of St. John’s are located in the south of Egypt. Many reefs of different sizes rise from the sea. A special dive site is the cavern system, Cave Reef. Divers explore the shallow reef formation through unique corridors illuminated by light rays.

sections.heading: Fury Shoal:

sections.text: Zabargad Island is around 3.5 km long with many interesting dive sites. A nameless wreck with a length of 70 m lies between 1 and 24 meters on the sandy bottom. At low tide, the mast towers over the water. It is possible to explore the bridge and the engine room. A hard coral garden on the west side and a colorful plateau in the south offer a great variety.

sections.heading: Rocky Island:
sections.text: Rocky Island is a tiny island near Zabargad. The legendary dive site is surrounded by a large fringing reef that seems to drop steeply to infinity. The reef is swarming with life and covered with lots of gorgonians, soft and fan corals. With a bit of luck, you can also spot big fish like grey reef sharks, white-tip sharks, and dolphins.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: The crew will transfer guests from the airport or hotel to the ship. A welcome briefing, cabin allocation, and ship orientation will take place before embarking. Guests can familiarize themselves with the vessel, set up their equipment, and get comfortable. General dive procedures and safety briefings will also be provided to prepare for the trip.

sections.heading: Day 2–6
sections.text: Guests can enjoy up to 3–4 scheduled dives per day, depending on the itinerary and sea conditions. Night dives may be offered when conditions and local regulations allow; however, they may be restricted or not possible on certain routes (e.g. offshore or Marine Park itineraries such as BDE). Each dive is preceded by a detailed briefing to ensure all divers are well-prepared. There are typically two experienced dive guides on board, maintaining a maximum ratio of 8 divers per guide, ensuring a safe and personalized diving experience.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: The final day of diving includes 2–3 scheduled dives, depending on the itinerary and timing, followed by sailing back to the harbor.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: After breakfast and check-out, preparations for disembarkation begin. The crew will say goodbye to guests and arrange transfers to the airport, assisting with check-in for onward flights.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: encounters with rich pelagic marine life and dramatic reef ecosystems. Divers can expect sightings of hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, manta rays, and large schools of trevally and barracuda in the open blue. The reefs are also home to vibrant soft corals, reef fish, and occasional turtles along steep walls and pristine drop-offs. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator. Sample itineraries and maps are for illustrative purposes only, and the exact route and sites visited may change based on local regulations, guest experience, weather, and logistics at the Captain’s discretion.

royal-evolution::Brothers, Daedalus & El.intro: Without any doubt the Red Sea is considered one of the most beautiful centers of attraction for sea and underwater lovers & one of the best dive destinations in the world, coming on the top of the wish list for any diver. The Red Sea is unique in several aspects: among them, its uniform temperature distribution at the surface and different depths. At the surface the temperature ranges from 26 to 30 degrees Celsius, and at a depth of 40 m. the range is still between 21 to 25 degrees, this’s one of the big advantages of allowing divers to dive any time all year round. As well the advantage of its high degree of visibility which reaches up to 45 m makes the Red Sea an ideal place for scuba divers & as well as underwater photographers & videographers. One of the most magnificent features of the Red Sea is its beautiful coral reefs and to be more precise, their skeletons, which are the main components of which the reefs are built. Different kinds of corals exist in different areas of the reef, the distribution of corals & their stunning colors reflects a breath-taking for all the divers. It’s the home of more than 300 coral species and more than 1000 fish species.

royal-evolution::Deadalus & Elba Reef (P.intro: Embark on a thrilling 7-night liveaboard adventure starting and ending in Port Ghalib, exploring some of the Red Sea’s most spectacular dive sites. From dramatic reefs to vibrant marine life, this journey is designed for divers seeking unforgettable underwater experiences.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Embarkation in Port Ghalib. Meet the crew, settle in, and prepare for the exciting journey ahead.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Start with a check dive at Shouna to adjust your gear and get familiar with the waters. Dive Elphinstone Reef for the 2nd and 3rd dives, a stunning site known for its colorful coral walls and pelagic species. Overnight sail to Daedalus Reef.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: Spend the entire day diving at Daedalus Reef. Encounter schooling hammerheads, barracudas, and a variety of reef sharks amidst the breathtaking underwater scenery. Night sail to Rocky Island.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: Begin the day with two dives at Rocky Island, famous for its vibrant corals and pelagic sightings. Dive at Zabargad Island for the 3rd dive, exploring its unique coral formations and rich biodiversity. Overnight sail to Elba Reef.

sections.heading: Day 5
sections.text: Dive the entire day at Elba Reef, one of the Red Sea’s hidden gems, showcasing pristine coral gardens and abundant marine life. Optional night dive at Elba Reef.

sections.heading: Day 6
sections.text: Continue diving at Elba Reef, discovering its untouched beauty. Night sail to St. John’s Reef.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: Enjoy two dives at St. John’s Reef, known for its fascinating caves, tunnels, and pinnacles teeming with marine life. Begin the journey back to Port Ghalib with a relaxing sail.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Disembark in Port Ghalib. Say goodbye to the crew and reflect on an unforgettable diving experience. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24hours before flying after the last dive. royal-evolution::Elba Reef | Elba border.intro: This itinerary has been specifically tailored for serious divers who want to enjoy the key reefs of the Red Sea in Egypt with no traffic, as was the case in the early 1980s, providing an ideal underwater atmosphere for all types of divers, particularly underwater videographers and photographers. Special permission has been granted to us by the Egyptian Navy to dive these pristine reefs and remote dive sites, which are completely untouched, including the famous Italian wreck Levanzo, a 113 m vessel built in March 1901 and sunk on 14th March 1923, lying on the beautiful Elba reef at depths of 22 m to 75 m. Please note that part of Elba Reef lies in Sudanese waters, and this itinerary covers a distance of 600 nautical miles.

sections.heading: DAY 8:
sections.text: Sail back to Hurghada. The Red Sea is famous for its plants and animals, many of which are related to those of the Indian Ocean, but some of which are exclusively found in the Red Sea. Among the common fish in the Red Sea are the Tarpon, Giant Herring, Salmon Herring or Milkfish, Soldier Fish, Goggle Eye, and Rock Cod. There are also more than 250 species of sharks, among them such veracious predators as the Tiger Shark and Hammerhead Shark. It should be noted, however, that unless irritated or attracted by blood, sharks are peaceful animals and, generally speaking, shark attacks along the Red Sea coast are very rare. In addition, several species of whales also find a home in the Red Sea, namely the Blue Whale, a 15 m-long giant that feeds on plankton, and the Whale Shark, which poses no threat to humans but scares off sharks. The Whale Shark, 8 to 1 Om in length, is a jolly, plankton-eating whale that befriends fishermen. It has to be noted that the Red Sea contains the largest collection of sea life consisting of Hard & Soft corals, Marine life & lot of Shipwrecks. safy-mar::Best of the North (Port Ghalib.intro: The Best of the North itinerary brings together some of the most famous and spectacular dive sites in the northern Egyptian Red Sea. Over six diving days, guests can explore legendary wrecks, colourful reefs around Safaga and the Sinai Peninsula, and the iconic Brothers Islands. The liveaboard usually begins with coastal check dives in the Hurghada area before the boat heads towards the northern Red Sea highlights. Depending on the port of departure, weather, and sea conditions, the route may include Ras Mohammed National Park, the SS Thistlegorm, Abu Nuhas, the Brothers Islands, Safaga, and selected reefs and wrecks around Hurghada. One of the highlights of this itinerary is Ras Mohammed National Park, one of Egypt’s most famous marine areas. Sites such as Shark & Yolanda Reef offer dramatic reef scenery, drop-offs, schools of fish, and colourful coral formations. The route may also include Mahmoudat, with the historic wreck of the Dunraven. Wreck diving is a major part of this liveaboard. At Abu Nuhas, often called the “Ships’ Graveyard,” divers can explore classic Red Sea wrecks such as Giannis D, Carnatic, and Chrisoula K. The reef is also full of marine life and offers excellent opportunities for underwater photography and night dives. Another key highlight is the world-famous SS Thistlegorm, one of the most iconic wreck dives in the world. This British wartime cargo ship, sunk during World War II, is often described as an underwater museum, with motorcycles, trucks, military equipment, and cargo still visible inside and around the wreck. Depending on conditions and the schedule, guests may have the chance to dive the SS Thistlegorm twice. The itinerary may also include the legendary Brothers Islands, located far offshore in the Red Sea. At Big Brother, divers can visit the famous wrecks of Numidia and Aida, both covered with coral and surrounded by rich marine life. At Little Brother, steep walls, gorgonian gardens, currents, and blue-water views create excellent conditions for encounters with grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, and, with some luck, hammerhead sharks. In the Safaga area, divers may visit the emotional wreck of the Salem Express, as well as beautiful reef sites such as Panorama Reef and Abu Kafan. The final diving day usually takes place around Hurghada, with possible sites including the wreck of El Mina, Abu Ramada, Giftun, or Shaab El Erg, depending on weather and logistics.

sections.heading: Highlights:
sections.text: Explore the best dive sites of the northern Egyptian Red Sea. Dive Ras Mohammed, SS Thistlegorm, Abu Nuhas, Brothers Islands, Safaga, and Hurghada reefs. Visit legendary wrecks such as Numidia, Aida, SS Thistlegorm, Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, Salem Express, Dunraven, and El Mina. Enjoy dramatic walls, coral-covered reefs, gorgonian gardens, wrecks, and night dives. Chance to encounter oceanic whitetip sharks, grey reef sharks, hammerheads, and rich reef life. Suitable for intermediate and advanced divers with at least 20 logged dives.

safy-mar::Best of the South (Port Ghalib.experience: Open Water - 20 minimum logged dives required.
safy-mar::Best of the South (Port Ghalib.intro: The Best of the South itinerary is a spectacular Red Sea liveaboard combining Egypt's remote marine parks with the northern part of the St. John's reef system and the beautiful reefs of Fury Shoal. This route is designed for divers who want to experience the wilder and more adventurous side of the Egyptian Red Sea, with a wide variety of dive sites, landscapes, and marine life. The itinerary includes some of the most iconic southern Red Sea locations, such as Daedalus Reef, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John's, Fury Shoal, Sataya, and Elphinstone Reef. Divers should be prepared for longer crossings, as the distances between the dive sites are greater than on many other Red Sea routes. In return, this liveaboard offers dramatic walls, remote reefs, coral gardens, lagoons, caves, swim-throughs, and excellent chances to encounter pelagic marine life. The liveaboard usually begins with check dives at Gota Marsa Alam and Gota Sharm. After the first dives, the boat heads into the open sea for an overnight crossing to Daedalus Reef. At Daedalus, divers can enjoy up to three dives, including blue-water dives with a chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, Napoleon wrasse, and other marine life. The western wall of the reef is known for impressive coral formations and the famous Anemone City. If conditions and schedule allow, guests may also have the opportunity to visit the lighthouse located in the middle of the reef. The next part of the route takes divers to Rocky Island and Zabargad, reached after another overnight crossing. Although the two islands are located close to each other, they offer very different diving experiences. Rocky Island is known for its steep coral-covered walls, soft corals, sponges, and drift dives along the reef. Zabargad offers beautiful reef scenery with coral pinnacles, passages, lagoon areas, and, in good weather conditions, the opportunity to dive the wreck of a cargo ship lying near the northern edge of the island. The liveaboard then continues to the famous reefs of St. John's, where sites such as Big Gotta, Habili Ali, and Um Khararim offer a combination of coral gardens, tunnels, swim-throughs, and natural reef labyrinths. Um Khararim, often called the “Mother of Holes,” is one of the most memorable dive sites in the area, with passages and coral formations that create a unique underwater maze. On the way back north, the itinerary visits Fury Shoal and Sataya. In the Fury Shoal area, divers may explore Malahi, a beautiful rocky labyrinth formed by tall coral pinnacles, and Claudia Reef, known for its colourful coral gardens and sunlit cave system. Sataya Lagoon also offers snorkelling opportunities and, when conditions are favourable, the chance to observe dolphins in their natural environment. The final diving day is usually spent at Elphinstone Reef, one of the most famous reefs in Egypt. Elphinstone is known for its dramatic walls, beautiful coral formations, rich marine life, and frequent encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks, depending on the season and conditions.

sections.heading: Highlights:
sections.text: Dive Egypt's spectacular southern Marine Parks. Explore Daedalus Reef, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John's, Fury Shoal, Sataya, and Elphinstone Reef. Chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, and Napoleon wrasse. Discover coral walls, lagoons, swim-throughs, pinnacles, and colourful reef gardens. Visit the famous Anemone City at Daedalus Reef. Snorkelling opportunities at Sataya Lagoon, conditions permitting. Suitable for OWD/P1 divers with at least 20 logged dives. Advanced courses and diving specialties are available during the liveaboard.

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: The southern Red Sea is one of the most biodiverse and least-disturbed stretches of ocean in the world. Its remote offshore reefs and marine parks shelter an extraordinary range of life, from the delicate feather stars and nudibranchs tucked into reef crevices to the powerful pelagic species that patrol the open water. Hammerhead sharks and oceanic whitetip sharks are among the most sought-after encounters, while grey reef sharks cruise steadily along the deeper walls. Napoleon wrasse – enormous, curious, and immediately recognisable – are a familiar presence at many southern sites. Closer to the reef, glassfish form shimmering clouds around coral pinnacles, attracting lionfish and groupers that lurk just beyond the light. Sea turtles rest on the reef flats, spinner dolphins move through the lagoons of Sataya, and the walls themselves are draped in soft corals of vivid orange and purple. Diving in the south means entering a world that feels genuinely wild, where the distances from shore keep the reefs pristine and the marine life bold and abundant. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

safy-mar::Big Five (Hurghada - Port Ghal.intro: The Big Five is one of the most exciting and prestigious liveaboard itineraries in Egypt. It combines five legendary Red Sea dive areas in one safari: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone Reef, Wadi Gimal, and Safaga. This route is designed for divers who want to experience the strongest highlights of the Egyptian Red Sea in a single trip, from offshore shark sites and dramatic walls to colourful coral gardens and historic wrecks. This itinerary is ideal for divers looking for action, variety, and encounters with larger marine life. Depending on the season and conditions, guests may have the chance to see hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, thresher sharks, barracudas, trevallies, turtles, and many other Red Sea species. The route also offers impressive coral formations, deep walls, plateaus, and wide-angle underwater scenery. The Brothers Islands are among the most famous dive sites in Egypt and are known for their wild offshore atmosphere. The area offers steep walls covered with soft corals, abundant marine life, and encounters with pelagic species. Divers may explore the legendary wrecks of Aida and Numidia, both covered in coral and surrounded by rich marine life. The Brothers Islands are also one of the best places on the route for encounters with thresher sharks, oceanic whitetips, barracudas, and trevallies. Daedalus Reef is a remote offshore reef and one of the top Red Sea locations for hammerhead shark encounters, particularly around the northern part of the reef. The site is known for blue-water dives, currents, dramatic walls, and multi-layered coral gardens. Its open-sea location and rich marine life make it one of the most memorable parts of the itinerary, especially for wide-angle photographers. Elphinstone Reef is one of Egypt's most iconic reefs, famous for its vertical walls, red soft corals, plateaus, and encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks. The reef offers spectacular underwater scenery and a true Red Sea classic experience, combining beautiful coral growth with the possibility of seeing large marine life in the blue. After the intensity of the offshore reefs, Wadi Gimal provides a calmer and more colourful contrast. This area is known for natural coral gardens, rich reef life, and peaceful dives in beautiful underwater landscapes. It is an excellent location for relaxed diving, photography, and enjoying the softer side of the Red Sea. The route also includes Safaga, where divers may visit the historic wreck of the Salem Express and beautiful reefs such as Panorama Reef. Salem Express is one of the most historically significant wreck dives in Egypt, while Panorama Reef offers coral-covered walls, excellent visibility, and abundant fish life. Together, they create a powerful and memorable ending to the liveaboard.

sections.heading: Highlights:
sections.text: Dive five iconic Red Sea areas in one itinerary. Explore Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone Reef, Wadi Gimal, and Safaga. Dive dramatic offshore reefs, colourful coral gardens, walls, plateaus, and historic wrecks. Ideal for experienced divers seeking an exciting Red Sea liveaboard. Suitable for OWD/P1 divers or higher, with previous diving experience recommended.

safy-mar::Central Red Sea Route (Hurghad.intro: The Central Route is one of the most diverse diving itineraries in Egypt, combining colourful coral reefs, dramatic swim-throughs, vertical walls covered with soft corals, famous shark sites, peaceful reef systems, and historic wreck diving. It is an ideal choice for divers who want to experience the Red Sea in a varied and exciting way. This itinerary takes divers through Fury Shoal, Wadi Gimal, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone Reef, Abu Dabab, and Safaga, with a powerful final dive on the legendary wreck of the Salem Express. The route combines adventure, marine life, beautiful underwater landscapes, and some of the most iconic dive sites in the Egyptian Red Sea. sections.heading: Wadi Gimal
sections.text: – The Wadi Gimal area is often considered a quieter and more natural part of the Red Sea. The reefs here are colourful, full of life, and ideal for relaxed dives. Divers can expect coral gardens, turtles, moray eels, lionfish, parrotfish, and large gorgonians.

sections.heading: Elphinstone Reef
sections.text: – One of Egypt’s most famous reefs, Elphinstone is known for its vertical walls, red soft corals, strong marine life, and the possibility of shark encounters. It is one of the classic Red Sea dive sites and a highlight of many liveaboard itineraries.

sections.heading: Abu Dabab
sections.text: – The reefs of Abu Dabab feature coral corridors, sandy areas, sponges, and interesting macro life. Green turtles, rays, and beautiful sponge-covered reef walls may be seen here.

sections.heading: Safaga – Panorama Reef and Salem Express

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: The Red Sea is one of the world’s most remarkable marine environments, home to over 1,200 species of fish, more than 10% of which are found nowhere else on Earth. Its warm, clear waters support thriving coral ecosystems that shelter an extraordinary range of life – from the smallest, most intricately patterned nudibranchs to the slow-cruising oceanic whitetip shark. Divers share the water with green turtles gliding over reef flats, spinner dolphins in playful pods, and vast schools of barracuda turning silver in the sunlight. Beneath the surface, soft corals in shades of purple, orange, and red drape the walls, while moray eels peer from their crevices and lionfish drift unhurriedly through the blue. The Red Sea rewards every diver, whether they are hunting for macro life in the sand or watching a hammerhead shark fade quietly into the deep. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

safy-mar::Fury Shoals and Daedalus (Port.name: Fury Shoals and Daedalus (Port Ghalib - Port Ghalib)
safy-mar::Fury Shoals and Daedalus (Port.experience: Open Water - 5 minimum logged dives required.
safy-mar::Fury Shoals and Daedalus (Port.intro: The Fury Shoals and Daedalus itinerary combines two very different sides of the southern Egyptian Red Sea: the remote offshore character of Daedalus Reef and the colourful, relaxed reef systems of Fury Shoals. This route offers a beautiful balance between exciting open-sea diving, shark encounters, coral-covered walls, caves, tunnels, canyons, and peaceful reef gardens. The liveaboard usually begins with arrival in Egypt, boarding the boat, and free time at the port. After departure, guests complete a check dive at a local reef before the boat starts an overnight crossing towards Daedalus Reef, one of the most famous offshore reefs in the Red Sea. Daedalus Reef is a small, remote reef located in the middle of the Red Sea, known for its impressive vertical walls, rich coral growth, and open-water atmosphere. The site offers excellent chances to encounter pelagic marine life, including hammerhead sharks and, with some luck, thresher sharks. Its dramatic walls and blue-water setting make it one of the most memorable parts of the itinerary. After Daedalus, the route continues to the Fury Shoals area, famous for its spectacular underwater formations. Sites such as Sataya, Malahi, and Claudia Reef offer tunnels, grottoes, caves, canyons, swim-throughs, and colourful coral gardens. This part of the liveaboard is ideal for divers who enjoy beautiful reef scenery, relaxed dive profiles, and underwater photography. Conditions permitting, guests may also have the opportunity to snorkel with dolphins at Dolphin House or Sataya Lagoon, one of the most famous dolphin areas in the Egyptian Red Sea. These encounters are often among the most memorable moments of the liveaboard. The itinerary also includes Elphinstone Reef, another iconic Red Sea site known for its rich walls decorated with soft corals, dramatic drop-offs, and possible encounters with larger marine life. The final part of the route may include dives at Abu Dabab and Marsa Shouna, where divers can enjoy calmer reef dives, turtles, coral gardens, and a relaxed ending to the trip. This route is suitable for divers with a minimum certification level of OWD/P1. Although it can be enjoyed by divers of different experience levels, previous Red Sea or liveaboard experience is recommended because some dives may take place on offshore reefs, in blue water, or in current-prone areas.

sections.text: Explore Daedalus Reef, Fury Shoals, Elphinstone Reef, Abu Dabab, and Marsa Shouna. Dive spectacular reef formations, tunnels, grottoes, caves, canyons, and coral gardens. Chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, thresher sharks, turtles, and rich reef life. Snorkelling with dolphins at Dolphin House or Sataya Lagoon, conditions permitting. Dive the impressive vertical walls of Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef. Enjoy the colourful reefs and swim-throughs of Fury Shoals. Suitable for OWD/P1 divers or higher, with previous experience recommended.

Depending on the season and conditions, divers may encounter hammerhead sharks, thresher sharks, dolphins, rays, and other open-water visitors. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

safy-mar::Northern Wrecks and Reefs (Hur.name: Northern Wrecks and Reefs (Hurghada - Hurghada)
safy-mar::Northern Wrecks and Reefs (Hur.experience: Open Water - 20 minimum logged dives required.
safy-mar::Northern Wrecks and Reefs (Hur.intro: The Northern Wrecks & Reefs itinerary is one of the most iconic Red Sea liveaboard routes, designed not only for wreck diving enthusiasts but also for divers who want to enjoy some of the most beautiful coral reefs in Egypt. This route reaches the northern part of the Red Sea and combines historic shipwrecks, colourful reef systems, marine parks, night dives, and relaxed coral dives around Hurghada and Safaga. The liveaboard usually begins with check dives in the Hurghada area, allowing divers to check their equipment and get comfortable before heading towards the famous Abu Nuhas Reef, often known as the “Ships’ Graveyard.” This reef has claimed several vessels over the years and is now home to some of the best wreck dives in the Red Sea, including Giannis D, Chrisoula K, and Carnatic. Abu Nuhas is not only about wrecks. These sites are full of marine life, and divers may encounter rays, barracudas, turtles, triggerfish, and, with some luck, even dolphins. The wrecks are covered with corals and surrounded by fish, making them exciting for both wreck lovers and underwater photographers. The itinerary also includes the famous Ras Mohammed National Park, one of Egypt's most spectacular marine areas. Dive sites such as Yolanda Reef and Jackfish Alley offer colourful coral formations, drop-offs, schools of fish, and classic Red Sea reef scenery. Night dives are another highlight of the Northern Wrecks & Reefs route. After sunset, divers can search for nudibranchs, crinoids, hermit crabs, feather stars, brittle stars, and other fascinating nocturnal marine life. One of the main highlights of the liveaboard is the legendary SS Thistlegorm, a British wartime cargo ship sunk in 1941 by German bombers. Today, it is considered one of the most famous wreck dives in the world and is often described as an underwater museum of World War II. Depending on weather conditions and schedule, divers may complete several dives on the wreck, including an unforgettable night dive. Towards the end of the liveaboard, the route visits the reefs around Safaga, including sites such as Panorama Reef and Abu Kafan, as well as the famous wreck of the Salem Express. This is one of the most emotional and historically significant wreck dives in the Red Sea. The final diving day usually takes place around Giftun Island and Gota Abu Ramada, often called “The Aquarium” thanks to its colourful corals and abundant reef fish. Depending on weather conditions and logistics, the final dives may also take place at other sites in the Hurghada or Marsa Alam area.

Visit legendary wrecks such as Giannis D, Chrisoula K, Carnatic, SS Thistlegorm, and Salem Express. Discover colourful reefs, gorgonian gardens, night dives, and rich marine life. Wreck diving course available during the safari. Suitable for OWD/P1 divers with at least 20 logged dives.

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: The northern Red Sea is a world apart – a place where history and marine life are woven together across the hulls of sunken ships and the slopes of pristine reefs. The wrecks of Abu Nuhas and the SS Thistlegorm have become artificial reefs in their own right, colonised by soft corals, glassfish, and lionfish, and patrolled by barracudas and trevallies. Rays glide across the sandy seabed, and turtles rest unhurried among the coral heads. Ras Mohammed, at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, is one of the richest reef environments in the entire Red Sea, with towering coral pinnacles, sweeping walls, and dense schools of snapper and fusiliers that turn the water silver at depth. After dark, the reefs reveal a quieter world of nudibranchs, crinoids, and feather stars emerging from the shadows. In the shallower gardens around Giftun and Gota Abu Ramada, clownfish tend their anemones and parrotfish graze on the coral, while the occasional dolphin passes through the blue. The northern Red Sea rewards divers with layer upon layer of life – historical, ecological, and endlessly surprising. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: The northern Red Sea and the waters around the Tiran Islands form one of the most ecologically rich corridors in Egypt. Strong currents flowing through the Tiran Strait bring nutrients that feed vast coral walls and attract an impressive range of pelagic life. Divers around Tiran regularly encounter large schools of barracuda, jack, and snapper moving through the blue, while reef sharks patrol the deeper edges of the walls. Turtles are a common sight, resting on the reef or gliding calmly between coral heads. At Abu Nuhas, the sunken wrecks have become thriving artificial reefs, inhabited by lionfish, glassfish, groupers, and moray eels. Ras Mohammed, where the Gulf of Suez meets the Gulf of Aqaba, is one of the most biologically productive points in the Red Sea – its reefs are dense with soft corals, gorgonians, and the relentless activity of reef fish. After dark, the same reefs reveal nudibranchs, crinoids, and feather stars that spend the daylight hours hidden from view. From the shallowest coral gardens of Gota Abu Ramada to the open-water walls of Tiran, this route offers some of the most varied and rewarding marine encounters in the Egyptian Red Sea. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive.

sea-friend::Sataya - Where Dolphins Touc.intro: Discover the magic of Sataya, a pristine marine haven in the southern Red Sea. This liveaboard retreat takes you to unspoiled reefs, turquoise lagoons, and vibrant coral gardens where dolphins, turtles, and a kaleidoscope of tropical fish create unforgettable underwater experiences. Designed for divers seeking a combination of adventure and relaxation, this journey blends exciting dives with serene moments in nature, allowing you to reconnect with the sea and its incredible wildlife.

sections.heading: Day 1 – Hamata / Embarkation
sections.text: Arrive at Hamata and board the liveaboard. After check-in, a safety briefing, and cabin orientation, enjoy your first meal on board. Depending on your arrival time, a short introductory dive or snorkel may be possible.

sections.heading: Day 2–7 – Diving Adventure
sections.text: Over the next several days, explore the southern Red Sea’s top dive sites, including Sataya Lagoon, Fury Shoals, Brothers Islands, and Daedalus Reef. Each day offers 2–4 dives depending on conditions and regulations. Highlights include swimming with playful dolphins, drifting along vibrant coral walls, spotting reef sharks and hammerheads, and photographing colorful reef life and macro species. Currents bring exciting encounters with pelagics, while shallow lagoons and sheltered reefs provide perfect opportunities for underwater photography and relaxed exploration.

sections.heading: Day 8 – Hamata / Disembarkation
sections.text: After breakfast, disembark at Hamata and transfer to the airport or your onward destination, taking home unforgettable memories of dolphins, sharks, and the vibrant marine world of the southern Red Sea. The southern Red Sea is alive with dolphins, turtles, grey reef and hammerhead sharks, and occasional manta rays. Reefs boast vibrant hard and soft corals, schools of fusiliers and snappers, pygmy seahorses, lionfish, and countless tropical fish species, making it a paradise for underwater photography and close encounters with marine life. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. Sample itineraries and maps are for illustrative purposes only, and the exact route and sites visited may change based on local regulations, guest experience, weather, and logistics, at the Captain’s discretion.

sections.heading: the Brothers
sections.text: offer breathtaking underwater scenery, wall diving along their entire perimeter and the possibility to spot a wide variety of pelagics. Their walls are covered in soft corals of all colors, black corals and forests of fan corals, creating a true feast for the eyes. Big tuna, shoals of jack fish and snappers cruise in the blue accompanied by hammerheads, grey reef, silver-tip, silky and oceanic white-tip sharks and mantas. The thresher shark, an oceanic species, as well as the magnificent Whale shark, occasionally spotted close to the reef, circle the walls of the Brothers on a regular basis. While diving in this part of the Red Sea also several times huge and spectacular moon fish have been spotted near the reefs.

sea-serpent-contessa::North Tour: Northe.experience: Open Water - 30 minimum logged dives required.
sea-serpent-contessa::North Tour: Northe.intro: This Red Sea Diving itinerary combines the most famous wrecks in the northern Red Sea with stunning walls and hard coral garden reef diving. Dive the famous four wrecks of Abu Nuhas, the Ships’ Graveyard. This reef lies close to the ship-lane toward the Suez Canal and has claimed more ships than any other in the Red Sea. The wrecks are very scenic, covered in corals and they are fantastic for photography, especially the Carnatic, having sunk in 1869. This Red Sea diving safari will also take you to Ras Mohamed National Park at the tip of Sinai, famous for its breath-taking walls rich in soft and fan corals and populated with huge shoals of fish. Nutrient-rich sediments from the Golf of Aqaba attract many fish species and also feed the coral polyps creating a paradise for divers. The very famous SS Thistlegorm and the recently discovered Rosalie Moeller are World War II wrecks and one of the highlights of this cruise. The SS Thistlegorm sunk in 1941, having been bombed by the Germans while on a mission to deliver a cargo of ammunition and war materials to the British troops in North Africa. The Rosalie Moeller, a British coal cargo, suffered the same demise only two days later. You will also visit the Red Sea diving reefs off Hurghada which are very rich and wide-ranging. A variety of colorful walls and hard coral gardens with plenty of colorful fish make them well worth a visit.

sections.heading: Day 1:
sections.text: Arrival and check-in. Dinner. First night onboard in the harbour.

sections.heading: Day 2:
sections.text: Departure around 8 am. Check dives near Marsa Alam coast. 2nd & night dive. Sailing to Daedalus reef overnight (7 Hours).

sections.heading: Day 3 - 4:
sections.text: Diving total 6 dives at Daedalus Reef. After 3rd dive on day 4, start to sail to the Fury Shoals (5 Hours).

sections.heading: Day 5:
sections.text: 4 dives around the reefs of Fury Shoals include the night dive (Claudia, Malahi, Maksour, Abu Galawa small), then sail to Elphinstone after dinner (7 Hours).

sections.heading: Day 6:
sections.text: 3 Dives around Elphinstone (if the weather permit), then night dive.

sections.heading: Day 7:
sections.text: 2 local dives then back to harbour at 3 pm.

sections.heading: Day 8:
sections.text: Check out after breakfast latest till noon. This diving safari covers the coastal section of the southern Red Sea offering stunning diving on a huge variety of reefs, walls as well as hard coral gardens teeming with fish life. Some of the best dives are made in the early morning when you are most likely to find hammerhead and grey reef sharks circling around the tips of reefs such as on the north plateau of the famous and exposed reef of Elphinstone with its sheer walls covered in soft corals. Shaab Sataya, the largest reef system in Fury Shoal, has it all – shear walls, ancient amphorae and yet another possibility to swim with big pods of friendly and playful spinner dolphins. The above itinerary is only a plan and it is to provide an idea as to which sites may be most likely visited during the trip. There may be deviations from this plan due to weather conditions, the captain’s decisions, the dive guides’ suggestions, the guests’ requests and qualifications and other factors that may hinder the safety of the crew and the guests.

sections.heading: Brothers
sections.text: One of the most amazing scuba dives, not only in the Southern section but the whole of the Red Sea, the Brothers Islands are quite isolated and thus a delicacy to be savored by the privileged few. They are barely visible and easy to miss, save for the Victorian stone lighthouse, a legacy of British rule, which towers some 32 meters above Big Brother Island.

sections.heading: Daedalus Reef
sections.text: Daedalus Reef (also known as Abu Kizan) is a 400-meter-long and 100-meter-wide (1,310–330 ft) standalone reef in the Egyptian Red Sea situated about 90 kilometers from Marsa Alam. There is a small artificial island in the center of the reef, which hosts a lighthouse constructed in 1863 and rebuilt in 1931.[4] Daedalus reef is a well-known place for diving because of good chances to see pelagic fish, such as hammerhead sharks, and an abundance of corals. In the high season, one can find many dive safari boats staying overnight, anchored to the reef.

sections.heading: Elphinstone
sections.text: This long finger-like reef runs from north to south in the open Red Sea. Steep walls drop to the depths on the reef’s east and west sides, while the north and south ends of the reefs are marked by a submerged plateau. Sharks often swim by the spot to feed on the abundant reef fish population.

sections.heading: SS Thistlegorm
sections.text: The Thistlegorm, on the west coast of the Sinai Peninsula and 40 km from Sharm El Sheikh, is the best-known and most popular wreck dive in the Red Sea. The 125m long British army freighter sank after just 18 months of her launch in April 1940. Her last voyage commenced on the 2nd of June 1941 as she sailed to Alexandria and was loaded with wartime supplies during World War II. A long list of inventory includes tanks, aircraft, armored vehicles, Jeeps, and Bedford trucks. Despite being privately owned and operated, the HMS Thistlegorm was nevertheless fitted with a 4" anti-aircraft gun and a heavy caliber machine gun when she was drafted for war duty, but it was never to be. In the early hours of 6th October 1941, the Thistlegorm was split in 2 and sank almost instantly after being hit by 2 bombs from a German long-range bomber. The hit only blew a hole in the port side of Hold no. 5, but then cargo tank ammunition ignited, causing the bulk of the damage.

sections.heading: Ras Mohammed
sections.text: Ras Muhammad National Park is located in Egypt on the Sinai Peninsula. It is found at the southern tip of the peninsula. The national park encompasses an area of 185 square miles (480 sq km). Along with the Red Sea Reef, there are two islands just off the peninsula that are part of the park’s protected area. On land, the park protects a small mangrove forest at the end of the peninsula. Further inland, the landscapes include mountains, dunes, wadis, and coastal mud plains. The Red Sea Reef and surrounding reef areas include both fringing and hermatypic-type reefs. There are over 220 species of corals accompanied by over 1,000 species of fish, 40 species of starfish, 150 species of crustaceans, and 25 species of sea urchins. The green turtle and the hawksbill turtle are two sea turtles that can be found swimming amongst the reefs fairly regularly.

sections.heading: Gubal
sections.text: Entry takes you straight to a sand eel garden, which you must approach with care to prevent the eels from hiding under the sand. There is a lot of life here, including thousands of tiny fish in the water near the reef, octopus, clownfish, parrotfish, and butterfly fish.

sinaistar::Brothers, Daedalus & Elphinst.intro: Experience three of the Red Sea's premier offshore diving destinations on this classic liveaboard route. Tailored for experienced divers, this action-packed itinerary delivers sheer drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, historic wrecks, and thrilling encounters with large pelagics — always with an eye on the open blue. Big Brother is a 400-metre-long island renowned for dramatic drop-offs and iconic wrecks: the Numidia rests on its northern tip at 10 to 80 metres, while the Aida lies along its northwestern edge, with every section of the island's walls densely covered in soft corals and gorgonian fans. Little Brother features an astounding concentration of marine life in a compact area, with vibrant overhangs, dense coral forests, and frequent seasonal sightings of hammerhead, thresher, grey reef, and oceanic whitetip sharks. Daedalus Reef, roughly 180 miles south of the Brothers, is a massive isolated reef encircled by deep vertical walls and dynamic currents, making it a premier drift-diving location where schooling hammerhead sharks, manta rays, barracudas, and open-ocean pelagics are regularly seen. Elphinstone Reef, a legendary Red Sea dive site with distinct north and south plateaus blanketed in hard and soft corals, offers world-class wall drifting and high-voltage pelagic action.

sinaistar::Deep South: Rocky & Zabargad.intro: Venture to the Red Sea's most pristine southern frontiers, where isolation creates unparalleled diving experiences. The journey takes you through the protected islands of Rocky and Zabargad - a sanctuary for dozens of seabird species and nesting grounds for sea turtles. These islands hold historical significance as ancient sources of peridot (chrysolite), though landing is now prohibited to preserve their fragile ecosystems. The route continues to St. Johns' spectacular underwater landscapes, where sheer walls plunge into the abyss, and massive coral pillars rise like a submerged stone forest. Some formations resemble Swiss cheese with intricate networks of grottos and swim-throughs. On the return journey, the Sataya archipelago offers opportunities to encounter its resident dolphin populations.

The Brothers Islands reveal their twin treasures—Big Brother's dramatic drop-offs where thresher sharks appear in deeper waters, while Small Brother's wreck-strewn slopes offer equally thrilling encounters. sinaistar::North Reefs, Wrecks and Tiran.name: 30% Off: North Reefs, Wrecks and Tiran (Hurghada - Hurghada)
sinaistar::North Reefs, Wrecks and Tiran.experience: Open Water - 10 minimum logged dives required.
sinaistar::North Reefs, Wrecks and Tiran.intro: Discover the world-class dive sites of the Northern Red Sea, from iconic WWII wrecks to current-swept wall drifts and thriving coral ecosystems across the Strait of Tiran and Ras Mohamed. The Strait of Tiran features four primary reefs positioned along a shallow ridge near the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba, where strong southwesterly currents sustain vibrant coral gardens and attract large pelagic species. Jackson Reef, the northernmost of the four, is marked by a cargo wreck on its northern side, with dives typically starting at the protected southern moorings past a dense forest of gorgonian fan corals. Woodhouse Reef, the longest in the strait, is usually dived as a south-to-north drift, its wall dropping to 30 metres before a canyon at 25 metres opens into a sandy coral garden favoured by eagle rays and reef sharks. Thomas Reef, the smallest of the four, is known for deep vertical walls and powerful currents, with a southeastern plateau at 25 metres where sleeping sharks are frequently seen. Gordon Reef offers a shallow plateau, drop-offs, and an eel garden on the sandy floor at 4 to 5 metres, marked by its lighthouse and the wreck of the Louilla. SS Thistlegorm, the Red Sea's most famous wreck, sank on 6 October 1941 after being bombed by German aircraft; the 129-metre British freighter now sits upright at a maximum depth of 32 metres as a thriving artificial reef. Abu Nuhas, known as the Ships' Graveyard, holds four wrecks along its steeply sloping northern wall — the Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M — with dolphins often seen on its sheltered southern side. Gubal Island and Bluff Point, near the entrance to the Straits of Gubal, are home to the wreck of the Ulysses and, to the south, the skeletal remains of "The Barge," a rich night-diving site. Sha'ab Mahmoud and the Small Crack offer a dramatic outer wall leading, via a sandy slope, through a 5-metre-deep natural passage into a calm, shallow lagoon. This itinerary is best suited to experienced divers, given the strong currents at the Strait of Tiran.

sinaistar::North Wrecks, Ras Mohamed, Ti.intro: Embark on a voyage featuring world-famous Red Sea shipwrecks, pristine coral systems, and renowned offshore dive regions. From the current-swept reefs of the Strait of Tiran to the oceanic walls of the Brother Islands and the haunting history of Safaga, this itinerary showcases the very best underwater landscapes the Red Sea has to offer.

sections.heading: Ras Mohamed National Park
sections.text: Situated at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, this world-renowned marine reserve marks the convergence of the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba. Known for vertical drop-offs plunging into the deep blue, dramatic pinnacles, and intense wall drifts, Ras Mohamed attracts massive schools of pelagic fish, barracuda, and reef sharks where nutrient-rich currents collide.

sections.heading: Strait of Tiran
sections.text: Located near the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba, Tiran consists of four primary reefs positioned along an underwater ridge: Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, and Gordon—named after the British cartographers who mapped them. Driven by strong southwesterly currents, these sites boast exceptional coral diversity and regularly attract large pelagic species.

sections.heading: Brother Islands (El Ikhwa)
sections.text: Rising from the deep offshore waters, Big Brother and Little Brother are legendary oceanic pinnacles. Famous for dramatic vertical drop-offs draped in pristine soft corals and massive Gorgonian fans, these remote islands are magnet sites for pelagics—including hammerhead, oceanic whitetip, and thresher sharks—as well as historic wrecks like the Numidia and Aida.

sections.heading: Ras Mohamed — Shark & Yolanda Reefs
sections.text: Two dramatic coral pinnacles connected by a sheer wall that plunges into the abyss. Divers can drift along the coral-draped wall of Shark Reef toward Yolanda Reef—a wide plateau dotted with coral outcrops that leads directly to the wreckage and famously scattered toilet cargo of the Yolanda. Keep an eye on the open blue for pelagics patrolling the drop-offs.

sections.heading: SS Thistlegorm
sections.text: The quintessential Red Sea wreck. Sunk on October 6, 1941, by German bombers, this 129-meter British freighter rests on a sandy bottom at a maximum depth of 32 meters. Now functioning as a thriving artificial reef, the vessel supports massive schools of pelagic fish and a dense variety of marine life.

sections.heading: Salem Express — Safaga
sections.text: One of the Red Sea's most poignant and historic wreck dives. Sunk in December 1991 off the coast of Safaga, this 115-meter passenger ferry rests on its starboard side at depths between 12 and 30 meters. The vast superstructure has become home to growing coral formations, pipefish, and schooling jacks, offering a solemn and deeply memorable diving experience.

sections.heading: Sha'ab Mahmoud & the Small Crack
sections.text: A vibrant barrier reef featuring dramatic outer walls covered in hard and soft corals. Dive along the exterior wall before following a sandy slope through a natural break in the reef. When the current aligns, divers can drift directly through this 5-meter-deep passage and break out into a clear, tranquil lagoon.

sinaistar::North and Brothers (Hurghada.intro: Combining the best of the Northern Red Sea’s historic shipwrecks with the adrenaline-fuelled oceanic walls of the Brother Islands, this route pairs vibrant marine park reef systems with deep-water pelagic action, tailored for advanced divers. Big Brother and Little Brother are two remote oceanic pinnacles rising from the abyss. Big Brother features sheer drop-offs, pristine Gorgonian forests, and two historic wrecks — the Numidia and the Aida — while Little Brother offers unmatched marine life density and regular encounters with hammerhead, thresher, oceanic whitetip, and grey reef sharks. SS Thistlegorm, sunk in 1941, rests upright at 32 metres, complete with its cargo of wartime motorbikes, trucks, and munitions. Abu Nuhas, the Ships’ Graveyard, holds four wrecks lying side by side on a sandy floor — the Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M. At the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, Ras Mohamed National Park features dramatic vertical walls at Shark and Yolanda Reefs, known for massive schools of fish, pelagics, and the famously scattered cargo of the Yolanda. This itinerary combines strong currents, deep walls, offshore exposure, and wreck penetration, so divers should be appropriately certified and experienced.

sections.heading: Highlights
sections.text: This four-day safari offers 12 to 15 dives at top spots such as Jackson Reef, Ras Mohamed National Park, and the World War II wreck of the Thistlegorm. You wish to combine your stay in Sinai with land-based activities while avoiding the crowds of daily boat diving. There is a variety of wreck and reef diving with beautiful coral gardens, drop-offs, endless walls, and colorful slopes rich in marine life, and a good chance to swim with dolphins. To dive the Thistlegorm wreck, divers must hold an Advanced Open Water certification and have a minimum of 20 logged dives.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: In the evening, starting from 18:30 H (6.30 PM) onwards, transfer to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and embark. Welcome aboard, cabin arrangement, and boat briefing. Permission to work with the port authority, sailing very early next morning.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Check dive at Temple. The next dive is Jackfish Alley, where you can easily enter the small caves. The third dive will be at the Alternatives, seven pinnacles with numerous sand patches and resident leopard sharks. If you like night diving, then Alternatives will be a great location to jump in.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: The boat sails to the wreck of the Thistlegorm and spends a minimum of two dives there. The first will be an outside orientation, and the second will give you the chance to look inside. The third dive of the day will be at Small Passage. A night dive inside the lagoon is possible here.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: The first dive of the day is the historical wreck of the Dunraven, which sank in 1876. The next dive site is inside Ras Mohammed National Park at the famous Shark & Yolanda Reef. Then travel north to the Gulf of Aqaba and the Strait of Tiran to do a third dive at Gordon Reef. Normally, the boat will spend the night at the South Lagoon, where a night dive is possible.

sections.heading: Day 5
sections.text: You start your first dive on Jackson Reef, the most Northern dive site in the Strait of Tiran. After breakfast, we visit either Thomas or Woodhouse Reef. The third dive of the day will be decided onboard on the way back to Sharm at either Ras Nasrani, Ras Ghamila, or Ras Um Sid. Return to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and disembark at 15:45 H (3.45 PM) latest.

sections.heading: Highlights
sections.text: For wreck lovers, we are concentrating on some of the best wrecks worldwide such as Dunraven, the World War II wreck of Thistlegorm, and the ship’s graveyard of Abu Nuhas with Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and the Kimon M. You will Dive - Eat - Sleep - Repeat for one week with 20+ dives. Magnificent old and modern wrecks paired with the best reef diving in the Ras Mohamed area. sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Early morning check dive at Temple or Ras Katy. The next dive is Jackfish Alley, where you can easily enter the small caves. The third dive will be the Alternatives, a chain of seven pinnacles with numerous sand patches and resident leopard sharks. Night Diving is very popular here.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: Very early in the morning, the boat will sail to the wreck of the Thistlegorm, the most famous of the Red Sea wrecks, maybe even worldwide. There is so much to explore, so the plan is a minimum of two dives. The first one is an orientation of the outside, and the second dive is a penetrating one. For the third dive, your boat will sail to Small Passage, where two channels cut the reef system of Shaab Mahmoud and connect the sheltered lagoon to the open sea. A night dive inside the lagoon is optional.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: The first dive of the day will take you to the historical wreck of the Dunraven, which sank in April 1876 - an old wooden wreck with plenty of room for passing through thousands of glassfish that live here in the shade of the wreck. The next dive is the Shark and Yolanda Reef, the southernmost tip of the Sinai Peninsula, with an endless wall unique in the Red Sea. Sailing back towards Sharm for your third dive at Ras Zatar, Ras Ghazlani, or maybe in Ras Um Sid. Return to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and disembark. sections.heading: Important Information:
sections.text: One needs to be an Open Water certified diver or equivalent with at least 15 logged dives. An Advanced Open Water diver or equivalent is recommended for some of the more experienced dive sites visited on this safari. You must have dived in the last year and recorded this in your logbook to join this safari; if needed, Scuba Review is available onboard. Open Water Divers can join night dives if they have previously logged night dives. This trip is suitable for snorkelers to join and snorkel at the allowed sites. Guests who have not been diving for more than 1 year before check-in to the liveaboard must complete a refresher program and have this signed in their logbook (adhere to the recommendations made by the certifying training agency). Guests can also sign up for an online reactivation program. The water part will be on board. Participation in diving activities can be restricted if the guide has any doubts about any diver’s safety and/or qualifications. The responsible dive guide on board may restrict diving activities in the interest of safety if the experience level or fitness is not suitable for difficult dives.

sections.heading: Sample Itinerary
sections.text: We do not announce a day-by-day plan but set up the best plan to cover all sites in the area, avoiding crowded sites and taking weather conditions and regulations into consideration.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: In the evening, starting from 18:00 H (6 PM) onwards, transfer to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and embark. Welcome aboard, cabin arrangement, and boat briefing. Permission to work with the port authority, sailing very early next morning.

sections.heading: Day 2 - 7
sections.text: The boat will sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive. The week-long safari will cover the area from the Strait of Tiran, Ras Mohamed National Park, and the Gulf of Suez, which is usually visited first. The National Park begins at the small bay of Marsa Ghazlani, followed by the larger and deeper bay of Marsa Bareika. Continuing along the coast to Ras Za’atar, Jackfish Alley, Eel Garden, and Shark Observatory, to the southern end of the peninsula with Anemone City, Shark Reef, and Yolanda Reef, and ending at the Quay. Because of the geographic position, this is a privileged area distinguished by strong, massive currents that transport large quantities of plankton and other food that give rise to an extraordinary growth of stony and soft corals and attract large schools of both reef and pelagic marine fauna, over a thousand species in all. Schooling barracuda, jackfish, tuna, and many kinds of sharks swim in these deep blue waters, especially in summer from June to August, sometimes early September. The safari will also take you to famous sites like the wrecks of Dunraven and Thistlegorm, Shag Rock, and the wreck of Kingston, sail to Shaab Ali where pods of dolphins are common, explore several spots at the Sha’ab Mahmoud reef system such as the Small Passage. Don’t miss the four famous reefs in the Strait of Tiran: Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Gordon Reef, probably the most interesting and richest in marine life. You can choose from several dive sites with superb walls and drift diving. In the afternoon of the 7th day, the boat will return to the Sharm area.

sections.heading: Day 7 evening / Day 8 early morning
sections.text: The last night will be spent at or close to the port onboard the liveaboard. Depending on the itinerary and/or administrative conditions, on week-long safaris, the last night might be arranged in a hotel. This is usually communicated in advance. Depending on your check-out and flight time, return to the New Marina (El Wataneya) port and disembark. Transfer to the airport or hotel, disembark at 12:00 H (noontime) latest.

sections.heading: The Brother Islands
sections.text: , the tops of two undersea mountains rising from the depth, are located about 50 nautical miles off-shore, near the town of Quseir. Part of the Marine Park, they offer breathtaking underwater scenery, wall diving along their entire perimeter and the possibility to spot a wide variety of pelagics. Their walls are covered in soft corals of all colors, black corals and forests of fan corals, creating a true feast for the eyes. Big tuna, shoals of jackfish and snappers cruise in the blue accompanied by hammerheads, grey reef, silver-tip, silky and oceanic white-tip sharks and mantas. The thresher shark, an oceanic species, as well as the magnificent Whale shark, occasionally spotted close to the reef, circle the walls of the Brothers on a regular basis. The huge and spectacular moon fish has also been spotted several times near the reefs.

ss-serena-dreams::North Tour: Northern R.name: North Tour: Northern Reefs & Wrecks (Hurghada - Hurghada)
ss-serena-dreams::North Tour: Northern R.experience: Open Water - 30 minimum logged dives required.
ss-serena-dreams::North Tour: Northern R.intro: This Red Sea Diving itinerary combines the most famous wrecks in the northern Red Sea with stunning walls and hard coral garden reef diving. Dive the famous four wrecks of Abu Nuhas, the Ships’ Graveyard. This reef lies close to the ship-lane toward the Suez Canal and has claimed more ships than any other in the Red Sea. The wrecks are very scenic, covered in corals and they are fantastic for photography, especially the Carnatic, having sunk in 1869. This Red Sea diving safari will also take you to Ras Mohamed National Park at the tip of Sinai, famous for its breath-taking walls rich in soft and fan corals and populated with huge shoals of fish. Nutrient-rich sediments from the Golf of Aqaba attract many fish species and also feed the coral polyps creating a paradise for divers. The very famous SS Thistlegorm and the recently discovered Rosalie Moeller are World War II wrecks and one of the highlights of this cruise. The SS Thistlegorm sunk in 1941, having been bombed by the Germans while on a mission to deliver a cargo of ammunition and war materials to the British troops in North Africa. The Rosalie Moeller, a British coal cargo, suffered the same demise only two days later. You will also visit the Red Sea diving reefs off Hurghada which are very rich and wide-ranging. A variety of colorful walls and hard coral gardens with plenty of colorful fish make them well worth a visit.

This itinerary takes you to some of the region’s most renowned dive sites, including vibrant coral reefs such as Panorama Reef and the legendary wreck of the Salem Express. Explore dramatic walls at Big Brother Island, discover famous wrecks at Sha'ab Abu Nuhas, and experience thrilling night dives that reveal a completely different side of the underwater world. sunshine::North + Safaga (Hurghada - Hur.intro: The North Wrecks & Safaga Diving Safari is a perfectly balanced Red Sea liveaboard itinerary that combines world-famous shipwrecks in the Northern Red Sea with the dramatic reefs and pelagic encounters of Safaga. This route offers an exceptional mix of history, vibrant coral ecosystems, and diverse marine life, making it ideal for both recreational and experienced divers. From legendary wreck dives to breathtaking walls and colorful reef systems, the North Wrecks & Safaga Diving Safari delivers a rich and unforgettable liveaboard diving experience.

sections.heading: Northern Red Sea
sections.text: The Northern Red Sea is renowned for its iconic shipwrecks, crystal-clear waters, and thriving coral reefs. This region offers a fascinating blend of underwater history and marine biodiversity, making it a highlight of the North Wrecks & Safaga liveaboard diving experience. Divers explore legendary wrecks such as those of Abu Nuhas, often referred to as the “Ship Graveyard of the Red Sea,” where massive steel structures are now covered in hard and soft corals. These sites are home to schools of glassfish, lionfish, moray eels, nudibranchs, and hunting trevallies. Nearby reefs around Gubal Island and Giftun feature coral gardens, pinnacles, and sandy slopes inhabited by turtles, stingrays, barracudas, and playful pods of dolphins, offering excellent wide-angle and macro opportunities.

sections.heading: Safaga
sections.text: Safaga is one of the Red Sea’s most diverse and impressive diving regions, known for its deep walls, strong currents, and encounters with larger marine species. The Safaga section of the North Wrecks & Safaga Safari adds excitement and contrast to the itinerary. Sites such as Panorama Reef and Abu Kafan feature dramatic vertical drop-offs, plateaus, and vibrant coral growth. Divers can expect sightings of grey reef sharks, white-tip reef sharks, tuna, and large schools of snapper and fusiliers. A major highlight is the Salem Express, one of the most famous wreck dives in the Red Sea. This historically significant site offers a powerful and emotional diving experience, now transformed into an artificial reef teeming with reef fish, batfish, and soft corals.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: : Boarding for the North Wrecks & Safaga liveaboard begins from 7:00 PM. After settling into your cabin, you can relax onboard or enjoy dinner either on the yacht or at a nearby restaurant. This evening is ideal for assembling and checking your dive equipment with assistance from the crew. The yacht remains docked in the marina overnight.

sections.heading: Day 2:
sections.text: The North & Safaga Diving Safari officially begins in the morning after final preparations and Coast Guard clearance. A full safety and dive briefing is conducted before the first check dive. Depending on conditions, diving typically starts at Shaab El Erg, famous for dolphin encounters, before continuing north toward Abu Nuhas, introducing divers to the wreck-rich waters of the Northern Red Sea.

sections.heading: Day 3 - 4:
sections.text: These days are dedicated to exploring the highlights of the North Wrecks & Safaga itinerary. Dives take place at Abu Nuhas, Gubal Island, Siyul, and Giftun, offering a mix of historic wrecks, coral reefs, and marine-life-rich sites. Expect excellent visibility, colorful reef fish, turtles, moray eels, and schooling predators. After completing the northern section, the yacht sails south overnight toward Safaga.

sections.heading: Day 5 - 6:
sections.text: The focus shifts to the best dive sites of Safaga as part of the North Wrecks & Safaga Safari. Divers explore Salem Express, Panorama Reef, Middle Reef, and nearby sites, enjoying up to four dives per day. These dives showcase dramatic walls, coral gardens, and increased chances of pelagic encounters, making this segment one of the most thrilling parts of the North Wrecks & Safaga Trip.

sections.heading: Day 7:
sections.text: Enjoy the final two dives of the North Wrecks & Safaga liveaboard diving week before beginning the journey back to Hurghada. After lunch onboard, the yacht arrives at the marina around 2:00 PM. Guests may disembark in the afternoon or stay one final night onboard to relax and pack comfortably.

sections.heading: Day 8:
sections.text: Check out is completed by 9:00 AM, marking the end of your unforgettable Northern Red Sea & Safaga Tour. Airport and hotel transfers are arranged according to individual travel plans. Beyond the famous wrecks and reefs, the Red Sea's clear, nutrient-rich waters support thriving plankton and small baitfish populations that attract an impressive range of marine predators. Divers may witness hunting behavior along reef edges, where jacks, groupers, and barracuda coordinate quick bursts through dense schools of fish. In quieter reef areas, cleaning stations are common, where wrasses and shrimp service larger species such as rays and reef sharks. The combination of warm water, strong sunlight, and healthy coral growth makes these ecosystems especially active, offering dynamic underwater scenes throughout the safari. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. sunshine::North - Tiran (Hurghada - Hurg.intro: The North of the Red Sea is the best route for wreck lovers. You will visit many wrecks, see the beauty of the underwater world of the famous Ras Mohammed National Park and Tiran Island, and encounter, depending on the time of year, frisky dolphins, notorious sharks, eagle rays, and magnificent mantas. Thistlegorm, Giannis D, Carnatic, Crisoula K, Dunraven, Rosalie Muller - these wrecks are familiar to all experienced divers and now it's time for you to see these world-famous wrecks personally!

The age of the reefs of these depths is billions of years. The rich underwater world sites of Ras Mo are in the top ten spots for diving in the world.
