topaz::Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elph.name: 10% Off: Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elphinstone (Hurghada - Port Ghalib)
topaz::Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elph.experience: Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.
topaz::Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elph.intro: This liveaboard safari takes divers to some of the Red Sea's most iconic offshore reefs. The adventure begins with the legendary Brother Islands—Small Brother and Big Brother—famed for their dramatic walls, strong currents, and regular sightings of large pelagics, including hammerhead sharks and dolphins. Next, explore Daedalus Reef, a remote marine park with sweeping walls, vibrant corals, and the chance to encounter schools of jacks, barracuda, and grey reef sharks. Its offshore location makes it one of Egypt's most thrilling dive experiences. The journey concludes at Elphinstone Reef, a must-visit for its sheer drop-offs, abundant soft corals, and frequent sightings of sharks and large pelagics. With challenging drift dives, pristine reef environments, and unforgettable encounters with big fish, the BDE route is perfect for experienced divers seeking adventure and the Red Sea's top offshore sites.

sections.heading: Possible Dive Sites on the Tour:
sections.text: Ras Disha. Wreck of the Salem Express. Middle Reef. Brother Islands. Daedalus. Elphinstone. Marsa Alam. Panorama Reef. El Mina Wreck.

sections.text: Check-in from 4:00 p.m. Welcome and safety briefing. Dinner.

sections.heading: Day 2:
sections.text: 1st dive - Ras Disha. 2nd dive - Wreck of the Salem Express. 3rd dive - Middle Reef.

sections.heading: Day 3:
sections.text: 1st dive - Big Brother South. 2nd dive - Big Brother (Numidia wreck). 3rd dive - Little Brother.

sections.heading: Day 4:
sections.text: 1st dive - Daedalus North. 2nd dive - Daedalus East. 3rd dive - Daedalus South.

sections.heading: Day 5:
sections.text: 1st dive - Daedalus. 2nd dive - Daedalus. 3rd dive - Daedalus West.

sections.heading: Day 6:
sections.text: 1st dive - Elphinstone North. 2nd dive - Elphinstone South. 3rd dive - Marsa Alam Area. 4th dive - Night dive.

sections.heading: Day 7:
sections.text: 1st dive - Panorama Reef. 2nd dive - El Mina Wreck.

sections.heading: Day 8:
sections.text: Breakfast. Check out by 10:00 a.m. at the latest. This southern Red Sea route is famous for thrilling drift dives, deep walls, and encounters with large pelagic species. At the Brothers Islands, divers often spot oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and large tuna patrolling the drop-offs. Daedalus Reef offers a high chance to see schooling hammerheads and occasional manta rays, while Elphinstone is known for its stunning coral walls and sightings of oceanic whitetips and grey reef sharks. Rich coral gardens, anthias clouds, and diverse reef life make every dive vibrant and exciting. This itinerary is ideal for experienced divers seeking big fish action and pristine reefscapes. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. topaz::Daedalus - Rocky - Zabargad - Elp.intro: This safari aboard My Topaz sails from Port Ghalib to the wild, isolated islands of the deep south – Daedalus Reef, Zabargad, Rocky Island and Elphinstone Reef – described as “wild landscapes and isolated sites, lost in the middle of the Red Sea.”

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Check-in day. Guests are able to check in from 05:00 PM up until 03:00 AM the following morning to get to the boat in time. Services start on Day 1 after check-in, and evening dinner is included on board. The boat leaves between 09:00 and 10:00 AM on Day 2.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Departure after breakfast towards the trip’s dive sites.

sections.heading: Days 3–6
sections.text: Up to 3 dives a day exploring the stunning reefs of Daedalus Reef, Zabargad and Rocky Island (and Elphinstone Reef, per the route name), in an order dependent on weather and conditions:

sections.heading: Daedalus Reef
sections.text: – On the northern side of Daedalus, a sunrise dive is offered on the reef’s northern falling, the side most exposed to sea currents and where there is the biggest chance of the most spectacular encounters with pelagics; it is not unusual to dive alongside schools of more than 20 hammerhead sharks, with carangids and tuna regularly present. From the deep zone, the dive continues along the falling, an exploration that demands close attention as it is full of holes and overhangs, with many black coral branches colonising the reef. While ascending, look up – barracuda are often seen riding nearby.

sections.heading: Zabargad
sections.text: – Zabargad Island shows fragments of rock resembling emeralds, which gave the island its fame and its name (Zabargad is the Arabic name for the green-olive mineral that once filled this semi-volcanic island). The dive site is characterised by peaks, canyons, caves and fallings, where divers may cross tuna, scorpionfish, leopard sharks, nurse sharks, angelfish, groupers, moray eels and blue-spotted stingrays. The island is also a nesting place for a large variety of birds, and during summer becomes a gathering point for turtles laying their eggs, surrounded by a turquoise lagoon.

sections.heading: Rocky (Rocky Island)
sections.text: – Five kilometres south of Zabargad, near the Sudanese border, Rocky Island is arguably the wildest dive site in Egypt: a shallow platform sheltering all kinds of marine life gives way to a falling covered by giant gorgonians, sponges and corals. To the south of the island is the meeting point for large whitetip sharks, grey reef sharks and manta rays.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: Dives are planned but depend on the flight schedule of the guests. The boat will be back at the marina in the afternoon; the last night is spent at the marina, with dinner served aboard.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Breakfast included; check-out between 08:00 and 09:00 AM. Guests can go straight to the airport to catch their flight; transfers are organised by the boat.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: Schools of more than 20 hammerhead sharks, carangids, tuna and barracuda at Daedalus Reef; tuna, scorpionfish, leopard sharks, nurse sharks, angelfish, groupers, moray eels and blue-spotted stingrays at Zabargad, which is also a bird-nesting site and a summer turtle-nesting ground; and large whitetip sharks, grey reef sharks and manta rays at Rocky Island. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. topaz::Dancing with Dolphins - Dolphin L.intro: 7-Night Red Sea Liveaboard – Swim with Dolphins, Explore Coral Reefs Escape the crowds and immerse yourself in a magical week aboard TOPAZ, our luxury yacht operated by Sea Pirates Egypt. Sail from Marsa Alam to the pristine waters of Sataya Dolphin Reef, where wild dolphins and untouched coral reefs await. What’s Included in Your Journey: 7 nights full-board on our luxury yacht TOPAZ Daily snorkeling with wild dolphins in Sataya Lagoon Visits to remote coral reefs, fish nurseries, and turtle habitats Optional free-diving and scuba diving sessions Guided excursions and eco-responsible marine experiences Stargazing nights on deck and stunning Red Sea sunsets On board parties

topaz::Fury Shoal (Port Ghalib - Port Gh.experience: Advanced Open Water - 30 minimum logged dives required.
topaz::Fury Shoal (Port Ghalib - Port Gh.intro: In this itinerary, you will pass magnificent sites such as: Abu Galawa and the Tienstin, which goes from the surface to 17 meters at the stern. A wreck of a hundred feet colonized by corals, to the point that in places it is impossible to discover the end of the wreck and the beginning of the reef (often on night dives). Sha'ab Claudio and large caves in the form of beautiful cathedrals that offer games of fairy lights. It is not uncommon in the morning to meet small white-tip sharks at every turn by a gallery, and most of the time a huge Napoleon wanders under the boat. Malahi consists of a maze of canyons where a magical atmosphere reigns, with beautiful lighting effects, also a paradise for photographers. Very often schools of mullet and yellowfin colonize the canyons. It is not uncommon to see a turtle ride in the water. Siyal Island is a small island of white sand where we stop to admire the sunset. It is inhabited by a multitude of birds, including beautiful fish eagles. We embark after admiring the sunset.

topaz::Get Wrecked (Hurghada - Hurghada).intro: This route brings together the most famous wrecks of the Red Sea. At Abu Nuhas, dive the Giannis D with its accessible engine room, the iconic iron ribbed Carnatic, the Chrisoula K (tile wreck) with easy hold penetration, and the Kimon M. North at Gubal Island, explore the barge for an unforgettable day and night dives, the Ulysses, and, conditions allowing, the deeper Rosalie Moller – a dramatic 2nd World War wreck. Around Shaab Ali, discover the legendary Thistlegorm, loaded with wartime cargo, then enjoy Shag Rock with its hard corals and the wreck of the Kingston. Southward, dive the scattered Yolanda wreck with its famous toilets, the upturned Dunraven at Shaab Mahmoud, and even the wreck of former liveaboard Fraser. At Ras Pieter, trucks and armored carriers from the Six Day War form a unique underwater museum. Your safari finishes in Sharm with transfers arranged for your onward journey.

topaz::Hidden Gems of the North (Hurghad.intro: This Hidden Gems of the North safari aboard My Topaz sails from Hurghada across the classic northern Red Sea, taking in Ras Mohamed National Park, the wreck graveyard of Sha’ab Abu Nuhas, the SS Thistlegorm, and the reefs off Safaga, with 3–4 dives offered daily (2–3 dives on the first and last day).

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Embarkation in Hurghada. The trip’s check dive is at Sha’ab El Erg – Level: Easy · Depth: 15m – a beautiful horseshoe-shaped reef where pods of dolphins frequently pass along the outer reef or inside the lagoon, and can often be observed while diving or snorkelling.

sections.heading: Days 2–7
sections.text: 3–4 dives are offered daily (2–3 dives on Day 7 as the boat heads back towards Hurghada); the order and duration at each site depends on weather and conditions:

sections.heading: Dunraven (Wreck)
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate/Advanced · Depth: 30m. This 80-metre British ship sank in 1876 after striking a reef near Sha’ab Mahmoud. Lying at 30 metres, the wreck is split into two sections with its hull upside down, now covered in corals. Divers can explore the open holds, home to surgeonfish, soldierfish and moray eels.

sections.heading: Ras Mohamed
sections.text: – Level: Easy/Intermediate · Depth: 40m. A natural reserve at the southern tip of Sinai, marking the separation between the Gulfs of Aqaba and Suez. The meeting of these water masses generates strong currents, and numerous pelagic species patrol the dramatic drop-offs – large schools of barracuda, snapper and more. We dive the park’s most iconic sites, Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, as a drift: descending along Shark Reef and its sheer wall plunging to –800m, then following the drop-off towards Yolanda Reef. Expect spectacular coral formations covered with soft corals and gorgonians, giant morays, napoleon wrasse, turtles, groupers and a huge school of batfish. The dive ends on the remains of the “Yolanda”, a Cypriot shipwreck from 1980 whose cargo – mainly bathtubs and sanitary ware – still lies scattered along the plateau.

sections.heading: Jackfish Alley
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 30m. An emblematic site of Ras Mohamed National Park, known for its spectacular underwater canyon. Diving from 5 to 30 metres offers a varied experience. Famous for its dense schools of jackfish, with frequent encounters with napoleon wrasse, barracuda and occasional grey reef sharks. The walls are covered with colourful soft corals and large gorgonians, with generally moderate currents, suitable for all levels.

sections.heading: SS Thistlegorm
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 30m. This British cargo ship sank on 6 October 1941 after being bombed by German aircraft while transporting ammunition and military supplies (trucks, cars, motorcycles and more). All these artefacts can still be seen inside the wreck – one of the most famous wrecks in the world.

sections.heading: Ulysses (Wreck)
sections.text: – Level: Easy · Depth: 20m. Diving the Ulysses wreck at Sha’ab Abu Nuhas offers a fascinating immersion between 5 and 27 metres. Covered in corals, it shelters groupers, moray eels and schools of fish; accessible to intermediate and advanced divers, it provides a captivating experience in the heart of maritime history.

sections.heading: Gubal Island
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 20m. The shallow reefs around Gubal Island offer exceptional visibility and host abundant marine life – colourful schools of fish, butterflyfish, parrotfish, moray eels and rays – with impressive coral formations featuring a rich variety of soft and hard corals. Nearby, Sha’ab Abu Nuhas (the “Ship Cemetery”) is a west–east oriented reef lying dangerously close to the shipping route linking Europe and the Orient; several vessels exiting the Strait of Gubal after the Suez Canal struck this fringe reef, and on its northern side five wrecks rest aligned.

sections.heading: Giannis D (Wreck)
sections.text: – Level: Easy · Depth: 20m. A 100-metre, 2,900-ton cargo vessel that sank in 1983 while travelling between Croatia and Yemen carrying timber. The wreck lies fractured but accessible, offering superb photographic opportunities.

sections.heading: Carnatic (Wreck)
sections.text: – Level: Easy · Depth: 20m. A 90-metre, 1,800-ton sail-and-steam steamer that met its end on this reef in 1869. It rests between 18 and 24 metres; its cargo of £32,000 in gold ingots was recovered, except for £8,000 still missing today. The hull is covered with hard corals, colourful soft corals and sponges, and inside, clouds of glassfish mingle with elegant lionfish.

sections.heading: Carless Reef
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 20m. An isolated coral reef and one of Hurghada’s most beautiful dive sites, with magnificent coral gardens. Drift diving between 10 and 20 metres, excellent for spotting grey reef sharks, whitetip reef sharks and eagle rays, with spectacular soft corals and gorgonians, and large populations of reef fish, groupers and schools of barracuda.

sections.heading: Abu Kifan (North)
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 30m. Offshore from Safaga, a legendary Red Sea site combining a plateau at 20 metres with a dramatic wall plunging beyond 100 metres. Famous for its colourful corals and rich marine life, including barracuda, tuna and sometimes hammerhead sharks. Strong currents may occur, attracting big pelagics but requiring experience; accessible by boat only, with exceptional visibility.

sections.heading: Panorama Reef (North)
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 20m. One of the most impressive sites off Safaga. Exposed to currents, it attracts dense and dynamic marine life; its vertical wall is covered with hard corals, sponges and spectacular gorgonians. The open-ocean atmosphere and excellent visibility make it ideal for experienced divers seeking thrilling, grandiose underwater landscapes.

sections.heading: Middle Reef
sections.text: – Level: Easy · Depth: 20m. One of Hurghada’s most balanced and enjoyable dive sites. This circular reef offers varied topography: pristine coral gardens, pinnacles covered in soft corals and wide sandy areas perfect for observation. Rich fauna includes butterflyfish, jacks, groupers, occasional turtles and clouds of anthias. Calm conditions make it accessible to all levels and ideal for both macro and wide-angle photography, with generally excellent visibility.

sections.heading: Panorama Reef (South)
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 20m. A more peaceful dive than the northern section, with calm conditions and a serene atmosphere. Its gently sloping plateau is covered with hard and soft corals and shelters abundant life: butterflyfish, angelfish, wrasse and turtles. Exceptional light and visibility make it ideal for underwater photography, suitable for all levels.

sections.heading: Tobia (“Seven Pinnacles”)
sections.text: – Level: Intermediate · Depth: 20m. A cluster of small reefs forming one of the region’s most enjoyable dive sites. Known as the “Seven Pinnacles”, it features coral towers separated by sandy corridors in a spectacular, peaceful setting. Shallow and suitable for all levels, teeming with life: butterflyfish, clownfish, moray eels and rays in crystal-clear water, and ideal for photography thanks to its vibrant colours and magical ambiance.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Check-out and transfer to the airport or hotel.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: Dolphins at Sha’ab El Erg; giant morays, napoleon wrasse, turtles, groupers and a huge school of batfish at Ras Mohamed’s Shark and Yolanda Reef; dense schools of jackfish and occasional grey reef sharks at Jackfish Alley; grey reef sharks, whitetip reef sharks and eagle rays at Carless Reef; barracuda, tuna and sometimes hammerhead sharks at Abu Kifan; and the resident groupers, moray eels, glassfish, lionfish, butterflyfish, parrotfish, angelfish and clouds of anthias found throughout the wrecks and reefs of Abu Nuhas, Gubal Island, Middle Reef, Panorama Reef and Tobia. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. topaz::North Reef, Safaga & Brother Isla.intro: This itinerary will delight shark lovers, dolphin enthusiasts, and those fascinated by stunning wrecks, coral reefs, and dramatic drop-offs bursting with colour. We will travel to the tip of Sinai before heading south to the Brothers Islands, famous for their spectacular drop-offs, strong currents, and encounters with large pelagics such as hammerhead sharks and grey reef sharks. This itinerary is best suited to experienced divers, combining diverse marine life, wrecks, and exceptional reefs.

sections.heading: Day 1 – All Aboard in Hurghada
sections.text: Board from 4:00 PM and settle into your cabin, followed by a welcome briefing from the crew. The boat remains in the harbour overnight; no diving today.

sections.heading: Days 2–7 – North Reef, Wrecks & Brother Islands
sections.text: Sha’ab El Erg: a horseshoe-shaped reef where dolphin schools frequently pass along the outer reef or in the lagoon — dolphins can be seen either while diving or snorkelling. The Dunraven: a British wreck that sank in 1876 near Sha’ab Mahmoud, its inverted hull now home to schools of surgeonfish, soldierfish, and moray eels. Ras Mohamed (Shark Reef & Yolanda Reef): a drift dive where strong currents draw pelagic species along dramatic drop-offs, ending among the remains of the Yolanda’s cargo of bathroom fixtures. The Thistlegorm: an English cargo ship sunk by German bombers in 1941 while carrying wartime supplies including trucks, motorcycles, and a locomotive, still preserved inside the wreck. Gubal Island: shallow reefs home to colourful fish, butterflyfish, and parrotfish, with a possible dive on the wreck of the Ulysses. The Carnatic: a steamship sunk in 1869 at Abu Nuhas, whose gold cargo was only partly recovered. The Ghiannis D: a wreck sunk in 1983 at Abu Nuhas while carrying timber. The Brother Islands: plateaus that are a major gathering point for grey reef and oceanic whitetip sharks, tuna, barracuda, and eagle rays, with the chance of hammerhead sharks and manta rays; strong currents suit experienced divers only. Safaga Reefs (Abu Kifan, Panorama Reef, Tobia, Ras Abu Soma): colourful coral gardens and abundant reef life on the return leg towards Hurghada.

sections.heading: Day 8 – Hurghada Disembarkation
sections.text: After a final breakfast onboard, check out by 10:00 AM.

sections.heading: Ocean Life:
sections.text: This route brings together some of the Red Sea’s most celebrated marine encounters — spinner dolphins at Sha’ab El Erg, grey reef and oceanic whitetip sharks patrolling the plateaus of the Brothers Islands, and the chance of hammerhead sharks and manta rays in open water. Expect turtles, napoleon wrasse, moray eels, and large schools of batfish, tuna, and barracuda around the wrecks and drop-offs, alongside vibrant coral gardens rich in butterflyfish, angelfish, and colourful reef fish throughout. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. topaz::North Reef, Wrecks and Tiran (Hur.intro: The Northern Red Sea is the best route for wreck enthusiasts. You'll visit numerous wrecks, experience the underwater beauty of the famous Ras Mohammed National Park and Tiran Island, and, depending on the season, encounter playful dolphins, infamous sharks, eagle rays, and magnificent manta rays. Thistlegorm, Giannis D, Carnatic, Crisoula K, Dunraven, and Rosalie Muller—these wrecks are known to all experienced divers, and now it's time for you to see them in person!

sections.heading: Day 1 – Check-in and Overnight on Board.
sections.text: Check-in from 4:00 PM. Overnight on the boat.

sections.heading: Day 2 – Departure for Diving.
sections.text: The boat leaves for diving in the morning.

sections.heading: Day 3-6 – Northern Red Sea and Tiran.
sections.text: Up to 3 dives per day to explore the northern Red Sea and Tiran. Destination route points: Umm Gamar SS Thistlegorm Chrisoula K (Marcus) Shark & Yolanda Reef RMS Carnatic Jackson Reef Giannis D Dunraven Tiran Tiran Island and Ras Mohammed National Park are excellent dive sites. The reefs at these depths are billions of years old. The rich underwater world of Ras Mo is among the top ten dive sites in the world. Butterfly fish, angelfish, Napoleon wrasse, seahorses, moray eels, barracudas... Can you imagine that? And that's what your typical day on board will be like!

sections.heading: Day 7 – Last Dives and Return to Harbour.
sections.text: Two dives in the morning, the last one ending around 11 a.m. Wash your gear and return to the harbor around 2-3 p.m. You can spend your last evening on the boat.

sections.heading: Day 8 – Check-Out.
sections.text: Check out from 10:00 am. The northern Red Sea offers an incredible mix of history and marine life, making it a dream destination for divers. Along the North Wreck and Tiran route, you'll explore legendary wrecks like the Thistlegorm, Giannis D, and Carnatic—now thriving artificial reefs teeming with life. Schools of batfish, barracudas, and snappers glide around the corals, while moray eels and lionfish hide among the wreck structures. In Tiran and Ras Mohammed National Park, crystal-clear waters reveal vibrant reefs where you might spot turtles, eagle rays, and even reef sharks. Depending on the season, playful dolphins and graceful manta rays often make an appearance, adding to the magic of this unforgettable diving adventure. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. topaz::North Wrecks Reefs, Tiran and Dah.intro: Experience the best of the Northern Red Sea and Dahab on this 7-night liveaboard adventure. Explore legendary wrecks at Abu Nuhas, including the Giannis D, Carnatic, and Chrisoula K, and dive the historic Thistlegorm, Shag Rock, and Kingston near Shaab Mahmoud. Explore the vibrant coral gardens and drift dives of the Tiran reefs—Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Gordon—each offering unique walls, overhangs, and an abundance of marine life. No Red Sea adventure is complete without the world-famous Dahab Blue Hole, where dramatic chimneys and colorful reef life await. The pristine reefs of Ras Mohammed offer spectacular drop-offs, soft corals, and encounters with barracuda, rays, tuna, and other pelagics. Whether you’re drifting along walls, exploring wrecks, or night diving under the stars, this itinerary combines history, adventure, and some of the richest marine life in Egypt.

The North Wrecks, Reefs, Tiran, and Dahab route captures the diversity and beauty of the northern Red Sea, offering everything from historic wrecks to vibrant coral gardens. Divers can drift along colorful walls teeming with anthias, butterflyfish, and parrotfish, while larger visitors like reef sharks, tuna, and eagle rays patrol the blue. The wrecks are now living reefs themselves, covered in soft corals and home to moray eels, lionfish, and glassfish. Around Tiran and Dahab, crystal-clear waters reveal intricate coral formations and the chance to spot turtles and playful dolphins. Each dive brings a new underwater scene, from dramatic drop-offs to tranquil lagoons, showcasing the incredible biodiversity that makes this region world-renowned. sections.heading: Daedalus
sections.text: Daedalus is situated 100 miles south of the Brothers Islands and is not really an island. In fact it is a huge circular reef with a lighthouse in its centre which hosts a group of soldiers like at the Brothers. A long bridge reunites this area built in the southwest part of the edge of the reef, where the boats come to moor. A beautiful excursion, when soldiers permit it, is a visit to the lighthouse, where the panorama on the top is unique! The possibilities to dive are numerous because of the size of the reef. The northern part is often chosen, when the weather conditions allow it, for the first dive at dawn and is an ideal area for large gatherings. Grey sharks and white tip reef sharks, schools of hammerheads, big trevally, and barracudas. Manta rays and eagle rays are part of the visitors to this area. There is also a wreck located north of the reef, but unfortunately off-limits to dive without special blends. The peculiarities of the drop-off on the west, besides the beautiful soft and black corals, are a huge colony of sea anemones with their clownfish in the more shallow area of the drop-off, a place that is also nice for snorkeling. The wall on the east side, consisting of madreporic formations, is also a place where all types of gatherings are possible. Near the bridge, the coral “pyramid” is lying, coral formations attached to the drop off at a depth of 8 meters that are rising to the surface.

sections.heading: Elphinstone
sections.text: At dawn we will reach the reef Elphinstone, the most spectacular reef that grows on the north and south. Four dives will ensure the very best of the Red Sea. Elphinstone North is a plateau that descends to 25 meters and that reaches the second plateau on 45 m depth with a nearly constant current. Pelagic fish and schools of hammerheads are often passing here. The east and west walls are covered with multitudes of corals, gorgonians and black corals, and a high concentration of benthic fish and corals. The drift dives are starting from the north and ending on the south side of the reef. Elphinstone South is unique below a depth of 25 meters, where the wall with a background of blue forms a huge natural arch that opens up at 55 meters depth and offers a very impressive sight. Sharks, tuna and schools of jacks are often present

sections.heading: Daedalus
sections.text: Daedalus has a large shallow reef with drop-offs at the sides. It varies from a few meters of beautifully clear water to the deepest point for recreational divers at 40 meters/ 130 ft. This means Daedalus has the best of both worlds. On the largely unspoiled reef there are stunning corals, tropical fish and huge Napoleon wrasse for divers to enjoy. In the deeper sections, out in the blue, the pelagics:

sections.heading: sharks, mantas
sections.text: and

sections.heading: tuna shoals
sections.text: can be seen passing through.

sections.heading: Zabargad
sections.text: Lying in Foul Bay just 5 kilometres to the southeast of Zabargad, Rocky Island squeezes almost all of the reasons to visit the Egyptian Red Sea as a diving destination into one tiny island. Surrounding the entire island is a convenient plateau that delivers excellent views during the safety stop. It should be noted that currents here can swing from the prevailing northeast, and shift to originate from the south. Current direction must always be checked while planning the dive. The shores of Rocky Island are split into 3 main diving zones: the south, the east, and the north shore. The itinerary and dive sites stated above are only an indication. There are so many interesting and varied dive sites that it is impossible for us to show all the possibilities. The captain and the dive guide will offer you the best dive sites from this region depending on the weather conditions (wind, waves, currents, visibility) and flight times.

vita-xplorer::Ras Mohamed & Brothers Isl.name: Ras Mohamed & Brothers Islands (Hurghada, Marriott - Hurghada, Marriott)
vita-xplorer::Ras Mohamed & Brothers Isl.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.

sections.heading: Day 1 / Saturday
sections.text: Arrival at Hurghada airport and transfer to the boat at the Marriott Marina in Hurghada.

sections.heading: Day 2 to 7
sections.text: Departure by boat from the Marriott Marina to Hurghada for a 6 day cruise. Package of 15 dives minimum for autonomous (2 to 3 / day, except 1st and last day of cruise 1 to 2) and 12 dives for supervised levels, in compliance with safety standards on the following sites:

sections.heading: Sha'ab El Erg:
sections.text: superb reef inhabited by schools of dolphins

sections.heading: Abu Nuhas, the "Shrine of Ships"
sections.text: Reef oriented west / east is in the sea route that connects the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean. Some ships coming out of the Gubal Strait after passing the Suez Canal hit the reef skimming the surface. On its north face are four well preserved wrecks:

sections.heading: The Carnatic:
sections.text: a steam sail of 90 m. long and shipwrecked by night in 1869. It is laid on a background of 24 meters. The story after shipwreck ... An expedition was set up to recover the cargo, 40,000 pounds sterling gold bullion! But were recovered only for 32,000 books, and thieves are still running at this time ... Diving side, it is a wreck light with delicate charm. The hull is covered with hard corals, multicolored alcyonnaires, and sponges. Inside, "glass fish", Pterois, Balistes, Javanese Moray, etc.

sections.heading: The Ghiannis D:
sections.text: Cargo of 100m. long, which sank in 1983 on a background of 28 meters. He was traveling between Croatia and Yemen and was transporting wood.

sections.heading: The Chrisoula K:
sections.text: Greek cargo of 100m. long and 3700 tons cast on October 30, 1981. It is layer on starboard at - 26 m.

sections.heading: The Kimon M:
sections.text: "The wreck with lenses" sunk in December 1978. It was carrying a cargo of 4500 tons of lenses during its sinking. Its holds are home to a large colony of hatchet fish.

sections.heading: The Rosalie Moeller:
sections.text: cargo of 108m. sunk in 1941 the same week as the Thistlegorm. A magnificent wreck, posed resting on a bottom of 50 m. The head of mat is at - 17m. from the surface. This wreck is plunging only in calm weather

sections.heading: The SS Thistlegorm:
sections.text: A bulk carrier of the British Merchant Marine built in 1940 by Joseph Thompson & Son in Sunderland. He was armed with a 120mm anti-aircraft gun and a machine gun. On his fourth voyage to Alexandria, Egypt, he was bombed on 6 October 1941 near Ras Mohammed by two German Heinkel He 111 bombers. The ship was carrying Bedford trucks, Bren Carrier snowmobiles, BSA and Norton motorcycles. , BREN Rifles and their ammunition. 303 British, various equipment and two locomotives LMS Stanier Class F8. Placed on a bottom of 30 meters, diving on this wreck does not pose any particular problem. In the 1950s, Jacques-Yves Cousteau discovered the wreck .. It has since become one of the most famous scuba diving sites in the Red Sea

sections.heading: Ras Mohammed
sections.text: declared a marine reserve in 1983 to protect its exceptional fauna and flora. It is a jewel of the Red Sea.

sections.heading: Brothers
sections.text: (small and large island) To name only the most famous!

sections.heading: Day 8 Saturday:
sections.text: Breakfast on the boat. The divers leave the boat around 8:30 in the morning. OKEANOSXplorer takes care of the luggage until the return time. Free day: visit Hurghada, souks, restaurants ... Opportunity to access a private beach with restaurants, shower ... This program remains the responsibility of our friends divers. Transfer to the airport. . This cruise will introduce you to the most beautiful wrecks on the northern route, the beautiful Sinai drop-offs at Ras Mohamed, before descending to the Brothers, one of Egypt's top dive spots. With such famous sites as Siyul Kebira, Gubal or Bluff Point, Rosalie Moller, Thistlegorm, Ras Mohammed, Big, and Small Brothers. This beautiful cruise combines shipwrecks, diving atmosphere and dives to meet the pelagic. The route is not completely defined and will be arranged according to the desiderata and climatic conditions, privileging security. It is a safe bet that we will visit these sites El Fanous, Turtle Bay, Shaab el Erg, Siyul Kebira Island, Shaab Mahmoud, Mohamed Rash, Small Gubal Island, Big Gubal Island, Umm Usk Shaab / Siyul Saghira Island Umm Gamar, Umm Gamar Shaabruhr, Careless Reef, Small Giftun

vita-xplorer::St John's Reef (Port Ghali.experience: Advanced Open Water - 20 minimum logged dives required.

sections.heading: ST. JOHNS'S REEF
sections.text: Before diving into the area of St Johns, we will visit the reef Abu Galawa and its main attraction: a small wreck with rich marine life. This reef is ideal for a check dive or on the way back as a night dive. The big reef

sections.heading: Shaab Sataya
sections.text: is also called

sections.heading: Dolphin Reef
sections.text: because of the many dolphins. This place is well known for its Roman remains, but, unfortunately, much of this is now gone due to the irresponsible behavior of some visitors.

sections.heading: Shaab Claudio
sections.text: consists of a maze of caves that are easy to explore due to the large openings on the surface, they are famous for their beautiful scenery. We will pass the tip of the peninsula of

sections.heading: Ras Banas
sections.text: , around the

sections.heading: Gulf of the ancient port of Berenice,
sections.text: and spend the night close to the island

sections.heading: Sirnaka
sections.text: where a wreck will be waiting for us.

sections.heading: St John's Reef
sections.text: is a huge reef of 21 km by 13 km lying below the

sections.heading: Peninsula Berenice.
sections.text: This area offers many dive sites thanks to the many "Habili". This is a name given by locals for reefs that rise up to the surface with a plateau situated between 60 and 80m from the bottom and that is only accessible via a liveaboard or mini safari. The drop-offs covered with gorgonians and black corals attract large pelagics: gray-tip and white-tip sharks, thresher sharks, and hammerheads. Manta rays, in the proximity of groupers and wrasses, offer an exceptional view. On the plateau, covered with the rays of the sun, a range of colors are coming alive and you will wish you could forever enjoy the beautiful sight.

sections.heading: St Johns Woods, Habili St Johns Woods, Gotta Wasta, Habili Wasta, Abu Basala, Gotta Hemera, Fendira Hemara Little Reef, The Nursery, Habili Omran, Erg Om Aruk, Habili Gafar, Habili el Radir
sections.text: are some of the reefs you might be diving during your stay. The final itinerary is not limited to the reefs mentioned above as we will also take into account the climatic conditions, the level of divers, and, of course, the wishes of our guests. vita-xplorer::Tiran & North Ras Mohamed.name: Tiran & North Ras Mohamed (Hurghada, Marriott - Hurghada, Marriott)
vita-xplorer::Tiran & North Ras Mohamed.experience: Advanced Open Water - 50 minimum logged dives required.

sections.heading: Ras Mohamed Tiran,
sections.text: also called

sections.heading: Best of Tiran,
sections.text: contains dives at different coral reefs until the Strait of Tiran and includes various legendary wrecks, such as the Thistlegorm and Rosalie Moller.

sections.heading: Ras Mohammed National Park
sections.text: is lying on the southern end of the Sinai Peninsula. It extends over 829 km2 of land and sea encompassing the

sections.heading: island of Tiran
sections.text: . The Strait of Tiran and Ras Mohammed involve the discovery of the fauna and flora of the Red Sea where you can only dream of. Napoleons and manta rays swim side by side in beautiful coral gardens. The appearance of white tip sharks in numbers before disappearing as suddenly as they came, is also common. Ras Mohammed has one of the most remarkable drop-offs in the world and with its steep walls dives are always surprising. The

sections.heading: Strait of Tiran
sections.text: has 4 beautiful coral reefs that fringe the surface:

sections.heading: Thomas Reef, Gordon Reef, Jackson Reef and Woodhouse Reef
sections.text: , baptized with the name of British geographers that mapped the reefs. Located in the middle of the strait, these reefs are often subject to a current, giving the chance to see much pelagic fish. The diversity of their corals is world famous and an encounter with a shark or turtle is not uncommon. A large wreck is planted outside the reef as a warning to ships passing by. Diving at

sections.heading: Thomas Reef
sections.text: , the smallest of the reefs of the Strait, depends a lot on the weather conditions, as at the north and south end of the reef very strong currents often occur. The corals are formed on vertical drop-offs and a wide plateau at the 25m zone surrounded by large gorgonians. This plateau is hosting, among others, sleeping sharks. Fascinating but take care of the current!

sections.heading: Gordon Reef
sections.text: has a different topography than other reefs. Diving can be done via a "drift dive" or via mooring and then be moving eastwards to the drop off at 16m depth. It is easy to spot a shark following the garden eels swimming in the current.

sections.heading: Woodhouse Reef
sections.text: is the longest of the four reefs. The dives are done via a "drift", generally from south to north. At the southern tip, on ca. 30m depth, a drop off is gently sloping and covered with coral homes of sleeping sharks. Divers have to be very careful in passing the place where the reef plunges beneath the surface in the direction of Jackson Reef, as it is a crossroad of several powerful currents.

sections.heading: Jackson Reef
sections.text: is the most northern reef of the Strait of Tiran. The dives are usually performed from the moorings. Boats are mooring in a zone with a weak current, facing a drop off of 40m. Among the most notable of the area, the coral garden with much aquatic fauna is amazing. The Strait of Tiran consists of narrow strips of sea extending over 13 km and separates the Gulf of Aqaba and the Red Sea. It separates the Arabian Peninsula and the Sinai Peninsula. It is named after

sections.heading: Tiran Island
sections.text: located at the southern tip of the Strait. It is a dream itinerary for dive fanatics. Abundant wildlife lives here: giant moray eels, napoleons, turtles, groupers, batfish beds, hard corals, multicolored alcyonnaires, and sponges. Inside, "glass fish", Pterois, Balistes, Javanese Moray, etc. As always these dive sites are provisional, as the decisions on the reefs that will be dived are depending on weather conditions and technical elements.

yachtiano::North & Tiran (Hurghada - Hur.name: North & Tiran (Hurghada - Hurghada)
yachtiano::North & Tiran (Hurghada - Hur.experience: Advanced Open Water - 25 minimum logged dives required.
yachtiano::North & Tiran (Hurghada - Hur.intro: Discover a spectacular mix of historic wrecks and pristine coral reefs, highlighted by the dramatic walls and strong currents of the Tiran Straits. This itinerary offers rich marine life encounters, vibrant coral gardens, and the chance to see pelagic species alongside classic Red Sea dive sites.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Arrival and check-in start at 5:00 PM, followed by the boat briefing, safety instructions, and dinner, with the first night spent onboard at the New Marina.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Departure around 8:00 AM, 2 check dives, and a possible night dive.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: 2 dives in Abu Nuhas and sailing to the Straits of Tiran.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: 3 dives on the Straits of Tiran islands and back to Ras Mohamed.

sections.heading: Day 5
sections.text: 2 dives in Ras Mohamed, 3rd and night dive at the Thistlegorm wreck.

sections.heading: Day 6
sections.text: 1st dive at the Thistlegorm, Shag Rock, and 3rd dive in Gobal Island, possible night dive.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: The final two dives take place in the Hurghada area at Umm Gammar and Carless Reef, followed by a return to port and the last night onboard.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Breakfast and checkout at 10:00 AM. Transfer to the airport or hotel in Hurghada.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: Divers can encounter schools of batfish, barracudas, and snappers, along with moray eels and lionfish sheltering among the reefs. The area is also home to vibrant coral life that attracts turtles, eagle rays, and reef sharks. Depending on the season, dolphins and manta rays may also be seen, enriching the overall marine diversity of the region. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator. Sample itineraries and maps are for illustrative purposes only, and the exact route and sites visited may change based on local regulations, guest experience, weather, and logistics at the Captain’s discretion.

yachtiano::North (Hurghada - Hurghada).experience: Advanced Open Water - 25 minimum logged dives required.
yachtiano::North (Hurghada - Hurghada).intro: Experience the northern Red Sea’s most iconic dive sites, featuring legendary wrecks, vibrant coral reefs, and encounters with dolphins. This route offers a perfect balance of world-class diving, relaxed sailing, and unforgettable underwater history, all starting and ending in Hurghada.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Arrival and check-in begin from 5:00 PM, followed by a boat briefing, safety instructions, and dinner. Enjoy your first night onboard at the New Marina.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Depart around 8:00 AM for two check dives at Sha’ab el Erg and Dolphin Reef, with a possible night dive in the evening.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: Complete 2–3 dives in Abu Nuhas before sailing to Ras Mohamed, with a possible night dive.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: Dive twice at Ras Mohamed, visiting Shark Reef and Yolanda, then enjoy a third night dive at Thistlegorm (no snorkeling).

sections.heading: Day 5
sections.text: Begin with a dive at Thistlegorm, followed by a second dive at Shag Rock and a third, plus a night dive at Goubal Islands.

sections.heading: Day 6
sections.text: Dive at the requested Rosalie Moller site (no snorkeling), followed by dives at Ulysses and Siyoul, with a possible night dive in the Hurghada area.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: Complete the last two dives in the Hurghada area, such as Umm Gammar and Carless Reef (no snorkeling), then return to port for the final night onboard.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Enjoy breakfast and check out at 10:00 AM, then transfer to the airport or your hotel in Hurghada.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: encounter schools of barracuda, batfish, and snappers, along with moray eels, lionfish, and blue-spotted stingrays. The area is rich in vibrant soft and hard corals that attract turtles and occasional dolphins. Reef sharks and eagle rays may also be seen, adding to the diversity of marine life in the North Red Sea. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator. yachtiano::Yachtiano Deluxe (Hurghada -.name: Yachtiano Deluxe (Hurghada - Hurghada)
yachtiano::Yachtiano Deluxe (Hurghada -.experience: Open Water - 5 minimum logged dives required.
yachtiano::Yachtiano Deluxe (Hurghada -.intro: A unique Red Sea adventure combining diving, snorkeling, and kiteboarding with nonstop fun, island hopping, and water sports. From dolphin encounters and vibrant reefs to beach BBQs and lively onboard parties, this itinerary offers the perfect balance of action, relaxation, and unforgettable experiences.

sections.heading: Day 1
sections.text: Arrival and check-in begin at 5:00 PM, followed by a boat briefing, safety instructions, a welcome dinner, and a party, with the first night spent onboard at the New Marina.

sections.heading: Day 2
sections.text: Departure is around 8:00 a.m., followed by two check dives at Sha’ab El Erg (Dolphin Reef) with opportunities for diving and snorkeling alongside dolphins, then sailing to Jubal Island for one dive, with a possible night dive, and an overnight stay in Jubal.

sections.heading: Day 3
sections.text: Start the day with an early morning dive at Jubal Island, then sail to Geisum to kick off the first kite session, enjoy a full range of water-sport activities, including waterslides, water skiing and wakeboarding, blobbing jumps, and sofa rides—and spend the night in Geisum with a BBQ on the island.

sections.heading: Day 4
sections.text: Enjoy an early-morning dive at Umm Gamar Island, followed by two dives at Careless Reef, kite sessions and fun water sports on Ocean Dream, before an overnight sail to Abu Monqar.

sections.heading: Day 5
sections.text: Enjoy an early-morning dive at the underwater military museum, followed by a relaxed dive and snorkeling session at Aquarium Reef, then a kite session at Abu Monqar and a scenic sunset on Abu Hashish Island.

sections.heading: Day 6
sections.text: Early in the morning, the boat sails to Salam Express for one dive, followed by another dive at Panorama Reef, before continuing to Utopia Island to enjoy an exclusive guest welcome, kite activities, snorkeling, and a night dive, with an overnight stay at Utopia and a beach BBQ.

sections.heading: Day 7
sections.text: Early morning at Tobia Arbaa, enjoy kite activities, fun, and snorkeling around Tobia Island, then relax and chill out before returning to port. The last night is spent onboard with a party and a surprise entertainment program.

sections.heading: Day 8
sections.text: Enjoy breakfast, then complete checkout by 10:00 AM, followed by a transfer to the airport or your hotel in Hurghada.

sections.heading: Marine Life:
sections.text: Expect encounters with playful dolphins, green and hawksbill turtles, and schools of reef fish such as snappers, batfish, fusiliers, and barracudas. Divers and snorkelers may also spot moray eels, lionfish, octopus, blue-spotted stingrays, eagle rays, and occasional reef sharks, all thriving among colorful hard and soft coral gardens. The last dive will be on the penultimate day of the trip. Divers are recommended to wait for 24 hours before flying after the last dive. (*) The itinerary description is provided by the boat operator. Sample itineraries and maps are for illustrative purposes only, and the exact route and sites visited may change based on local regulations, guest experience, weather, and logistics at the Captain’s discretion.
